title: Copyright headers: Posit for files the fork added
description:
## Problem

The fork started by integrating SAS's VS Code extension into Positron, and has since added its own features: the Positron integration, Clinical Acceleration, LSAF, background jobs and more. New files were started from SAS's header template, so 210 files we added say `Copyright © 20xx, SAS Institute Inc.`.

## Change

Header lines only; the `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` line stays the same.

| Group | Files | Header |
|---|---|---|
| Written by Posit staff (Michael Mayer; `css.d.ts` by Jon Vanausdeln) | 197 | `// Copyright © 2026, Posit Software, PBC. All Rights Reserved.` replaces the SAS line |
| Ported from SAS's `vscode-sas-ca-extension`: `client/src/clinical/{RepositoryDataProvider,RepositoryDecorator,RepositoryModel,actionStatus,const,index,messages,types,utils}.ts` | 9 | SAS 2024 line kept, Posit line added below it |
| stdio connection contributed by Andreas Menrath (Analytical Software): `client/src/connection/stdio/*`, `client/test/connection/stdio/index.test.ts` | 4 | unchanged (SAS) |
| Every file that exists in upstream v1.21.0 | — | unchanged |

**How the list was built:**
- The candidates are the files added since the upstream base: `git diff --diff-filter=A v1.21.0 HEAD`.
- From those, I kept the ones whose first line is the SAS header, and grouped them by the author of the commit that added each file.
- I compared each file's lines against upstream v1.21.0 and the CA extension. Apart from the CA ports, no file shares substantive code: the highest is 27%, generic VS Code idioms.

Upstream has none of these paths (checked against `upstream/main`, 2026-11-19), so this doesn't affect upstream syncs. Files without any header (images, json, md, a few .mjs/.tsx/.yml files) are left as they are.

## Testing

- `git diff --numstat`: 197 files `1 1`, 9 files `1 0`, nothing else.
- No touched file exists in `v1.21.0`. Among the added files, only the 9 dual-header and 4 stdio files still name SAS.
- `npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit -p client` pass.

title: Positron: declare the SAS language runtime in the manifest
description:
## Problem

In review of quarto-dev/quarto#1237, the Quarto maintainers asked Quarto to decide which cells can run from the `languageRuntimes` manifest contribution, the source Positron already uses for inline output (`hasLanguageRuntimeProvider`). Registered runtimes would be only a second source. A runtime registers only after its extension activates and finds a profile, so without the contribution `{sas}` cells aren't runnable before a SAS connection profile exists. The SAS extension doesn't declare the contribution yet; the R, Python and ggsql extensions do.

## Change

- `package.json`: `"languageRuntimes": [{ "languageId": "sas" }]`. One key added; nothing else in the file is reformatted.
- **Recommended runtime is now Explicit.** With the contribution, Positron counts `sas` as a language pack. It activates the extension at startup (`onLanguageRuntime:sas`) and asks it for a recommended runtime. `recommendedWorkspaceRuntime()` returned the active profile with `startupBehavior: Implicit`. Positron starts an Implicit recommendation when a `.sas` file opens, and an affiliation saved from it could start at launch, since `startAffiliatedLanguageRuntimes` skips only never-started **Explicit** ones. Either way it would connect to Viya and ask to sign in without anyone asking. The recommendation is now Explicit, like the discovered runtimes. The supervisor manager already used Explicit.
- Docs: `Features/positron.md` notes the upcoming Quarto change and that the stopgap lenses (#163) will step aside for that Quarto version. The CHANGELOG has an entry.

Until a Quarto release includes #1237, `{sas}` chunks run only through our own lenses and commands from #163, as today. This PR and the Quarto change can ship in either order.

## Testing

- `tsc` and eslint pass for the client. Prettier flags import order in `PositronLanguageRuntimeManager.ts`, but `main` already has the same issue, so I left it alone.
- **Manual test in Positron 2026.12 (VS Code 1.143).** I used a separate profile with this branch's VSIX, a VSIX of quarto-dev/quarto#1237, and ggsql 0.5.2:
  - Inline output off:
    - `{sas}` and `{ggsql}` cells show Quarto's lenses before any console exists. `{sas}` cells also show our stopgap's, as expected for now.
    - Cmd+Shift+Enter, Cmd+Enter, Run Next Cell and Run Above run in the right console.
    - The `*| …;` and `#|` option lines are not sent.
  - Inline output on: both languages run.

## Follow-up

Once a Quarto release includes #1237, hide the stopgap lenses for that version (TODO in `quartoSasCells.ts`). Also hide them while inline output is on: they still show then, and they run in the console instead of inline.

title: SAS Life Science Analytics Framework (LSAF) support
description:
## Summary

This adds support for SAS Life Science Analytics Framework (LSAF) through the LSAF REST API 1.0. The new **LSAF** sidebar has **Repository**, **Workspace** and **Jobs** views.

> [!WARNING]
> **Not tested against a live LSAF server.** The code was built from the API's OpenAPI document and tested against a local mock of it (`client/test/lsaf-mock/server.ts`). Where the spec is unclear, the code guesses; see the live-check list below.

### Detection and sign-in
- LSAF is independent of the SAS connection profiles. It is configured with `SAS.lsaf.url`, or `SAS_LSAF_URL` for Workbench admins.
- **Nothing LSAF shows unless that URL answers like LSAF.** The extension calls `/apiMeta` and `/` without signing in, and accepts JSON or an LSAF error body (`SAS.lsaf.available`). It retries while the server doesn't answer.
- **Sign In** asks for the user ID and password once. It calls `GET /encrypt` and keeps only the `{P21}` encrypted password in SecretStorage. When a request gets a 401 (the session timed out), it signs on again with that password and replays the request.
- When LSAF is detected and there is no SAS profile, the SAS sidebar no longer shows a **Sign In** that can only ask for a profile. This uses a new context key, `SAS.hasActiveProfile`.

### Repository and Workspace
- **Repository:**
  - Browse contexts, folders and files, and open files and their versions read-only (`sasLsaf:`). Datasets open in the Data Explorer.
  - **Properties** shows details, versions and signatures in the Viewer.
  - **Version History** opens or compares a version.
  - **Download** saves a file, or a folder as a zip.
  - Checked-out files show a **CO** badge.
- **Workspace:** an editable file system (`sasLsafWorkspace:`).
  - Each workspace folder is also listed in the repository at the same path, to show check-out and versioning state.
  - Actions: Check Out (keep or replace the workspace copy), Check In (comment, and the next major, minor or a specific version), Undo Check Out, Copy to Workspace, Add to Repository, Compare with Repository, Upload, New File and New Folder.

### Jobs
- **Run Job** and **Run Job with Parameters...** run a `.job` file from either view or from its editor.
- **Run on LSAF**, in the Run menu of a workspace `.sas` file, creates `<program>.job` next to the program and runs it.
- The **Jobs** view lists runs and polls them (from 3 s, backing off to 15 s). When a run finishes, a notification offers its log and manifest. Runs are kept locally per server and user, because the API can't list them.

### Docs
- New page `website/docs/Features/lsaf.md`, with a table of **what the LSAF REST API can't do** and the workaround for each: delete, rename and create folders; list or cancel runs; read job parameters; manifest and log formats; paging; permissions.
- Also updated: the `positron.md` section and feature matrix row, both READMEs, and the CHANGELOG.
- New Posit Assistant skill: `assistant-skills/sas-lsaf`.

### Shared code touched
- `ReportPresenter` gains an optional `linkSchemes` argument. Clinical Acceleration behaves as before.
- `node/extension.ts` registers LSAF and sets `SAS.hasActiveProfile`.
- One `when` clause on the upstream view `sas-content-get-started`.

## Test plan
- [x] `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 717 passing, 62 of them new LSAF tests (`client/test/positron/lsaf*.test.ts`), covering:
  - paths;
  - the client (logon, 401 replay, error bodies, 200-with-warning results);
  - the probe classifier;
  - context values against the `package.json` menus;
  - guards that every LSAF view and palette or editor entry requires `SAS.lsaf.available`;
  - the repository, workspace and job models over real HTTP against the mock;
  - the zip writer;
  - the manifest parser and the run store.
- [x] Lint, `npm run compile`, `tsc -p client` (no errors) and `docusaurus build` all pass.
- [x] Clicked through in Positron with the VSIX against the mock server (`npx ts-node --transpile-only client/test/lsaf-mock/server.ts 8765`, `SAS.lsaf.url=http://127.0.0.1:8765/lsaf/api`, user `demo` / `demo`).
- [x] The empty-folder zip that New Folder uploads opens as valid in Python's `zipfile` and in `unzip`.

### Live check, for the first person with LSAF access
- [ ] Detection: `/apiMeta` without a token gives an LSAF error body or JSON.
- [ ] `/encrypt` response shape: a bare string, `{encryptedPassword}` or plain text are all handled. Logon with the `{P21}` password.
- [ ] Top-level listing at `/repository/containers?component=children` and `/workspace/folders?component=children`, with no path.
- [ ] `limit=10000` is accepted for children.
- [ ] Repository `action=checkin` with an empty multipart body (the spec lists one).
- [ ] New Folder: `PUT /workspace/folders/{parent}` with a multipart `uploadFile` zip.
- [ ] Job creation: `POST /jobs/workspace/{path}` with `["./prog.sas"]` and `useRelativePaths=true`.
- [ ] Submission `state` values beyond `completed`: failure, warnings and cancel.
- [ ] Manifest format, and whether the log is found from it (otherwise the fallback picks up new `.log` files in the job's folder).
- [ ] Repository job runs check their outputs in.

title: Positron: run {sas} chunks of Quarto documents in the SAS console
description:
## Problem

In a Quarto document with `{sas}` chunks (sasquatch), the full render works, but you can't run a single chunk interactively. The Quarto extension (1.139) only runs R, Python, Julia and C# cells in Positron (`cellExecutorForLanguage` in its Positron host). So `{sas}` chunks get no **Run Cell** lens, and Cmd+Shift+Enter on them does nothing.

## Change

- `{sas}` chunks get **Run Cell**, **Run Next Cell** and **Run Above** lenses, with the labels Quarto uses. The code runs in the SAS console: the log goes to the console and results to the Viewer, and a console starts if none is running. Leading `*|` chunk-option lines are not sent.
- Commands in the Command Palette:
  - `SAS.quarto.runCell`
  - `SAS.quarto.runNextCell`
  - `SAS.quarto.runCellsAbove`
  - `SAS.quarto.runCellsBelow`
  - `SAS.quarto.runCurrent`, which runs the selection or, without one, the whole chunk
- The parser is the pure `quartoSasChunks.ts`, with unit tests. The VS Code wiring is in `quartoSasCells.ts`.
- **No default keybindings.** Positron weighs an extension's keybindings as `400 + index in its own list`, and the highest wins. Quarto's Cmd+Enter (index 8) and Cmd+Shift+Enter (index 12) therefore always beat ours, and on `{sas}` chunks they do nothing. The docs give a `keybindings.json` snippet that uses the new `SAS.inQuartoSasCell` context key.
- Docs: a new section "SAS Chunks in Quarto Documents" in `Features/positron.md`, a Known Limitations row (source editor only), and a CHANGELOG entry. The docs note that the console is not the saspy session sasquatch uses to render.

## Long-term fix

The upstream Quarto PR makes Quarto run cells in any language that has a Positron runtime. That gives `{sas}` Quarto's own lenses and shortcuts. Once a Quarto release includes it, these lenses should be hidden for that version so chunks don't show two Run Cell lenses; there's a TODO in `quartoSasCells.ts`.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 9 new tests pass.
- eslint, prettier and `npm run compile` pass.
- Checked by hand in Positron with a packaged VSIX on `report-1.qmd`: the lenses appear only on `{sas}` chunks, and Run Cell and Run Above run in the SAS console.

title: Choose the compute context of a SAS Viya console
description:
Choose the **SAS Viya compute context** of the SAS console, as background jobs already can, and see which context a console runs in.

## What's in it

- **Choose Compute Context...**: a server icon in the Console title bar, next to the SAS log filter, and in the Command Palette. It shows only while a SAS Viya console is in front. It lists the server's compute contexts, current one first. If they can't be listed, a name can be typed in.
- **The choice is the Viya profile's `context`**, the setting every interactive session of the profile already uses: consoles, notebooks, the SAS Content and SAS Server views. Background jobs follow it unless `SAS.backgroundJobs.computeContext` is set.
- **Restart Now / Later**: after the choice, a message offers to replace the console with a new one in the new context. Replacing it loses WORK and macro variables.
- **The console shows its context.** The console tab and the header of the Console Information popup read `Viya · SAS Studio`: the profile name, then the context without " compute context". The console's start-up line names the full context.

SAS Viya only. SAS 9.4 consoles (`ssh`, `com`, `iom`, `stdio`), and Viya profiles that connect to a running server (`serverId`, which bypasses contexts), get no icon and keep their old name.

## Why a new console rather than a restart

Positron reads a session's name only when the session is created (`createSession` / `restoreSession`). An in-place restart never re-reads it, and there's no API to rename a session. Also, Positron's console action bar (Restart, Information, ...) doesn't take extension buttons, so the icon goes in the panel's title bar instead. So:

- **Each console keeps the context it was created with.** Positron's toolbar Restart restarts it in that context, so its name always matches where it runs.
- **Restart Now** deletes the session and starts a new one for the same runtime, which runs in, and is named after, the new context.

## Files shared with upstream

Touched minimally, to keep upstream merges clean:
- `package.json`: insertions only, for the command, a `view/title` entry and a Command Palette entry.
- `package.nls.json`: one appended key.
- `client/src/connection/index.ts`: `createSessionForProfile` (fork-added) takes an optional context override.

## Tests

- `npm run test-positron`: 646 passing, including 6 new tests for the context rules, the short name, the start-up line, and how the profile is saved.
- Lint clean. The build and the docs site build succeed.
- Tried in Positron against a live SAS Viya server:
  - The name and info header show the context.
  - Restart Now opens a new console in the chosen context.
  - With Later, the toolbar Restart keeps the console's context.
  - No icon appears for non-Viya consoles.

title: SAS Viya background jobs, saved SAS jobs, and schedules
description:
Closes #150.

Submit SAS programs as **SAS Viya background jobs**, the way SAS Studio's Background Submit does, save them as reusable **SAS jobs** with parameters, and **schedule** them. Jobs run on the server in their own compute server through the Job Execution service, so the SAS console stays free and work keeps running when Positron closes.

## Which SAS products

SAS Viya only. SAS 9.4 connections (`ssh`, `com`, `iom`, `stdio`) have no job service, so nothing appears for them. Within Viya each part is gated on what the server actually runs, by probing the service roots:

| Context key | Probe | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `SAS.backgroundJobsAvailable` | `/jobExecution/` | submitting, the **Background Jobs** view |
| `SAS.jobDefinitionsAvailable` | `/jobDefinitions/` | **Save as SAS Job**, the **SAS Jobs** view |
| `SAS.jobSchedulingAvailable` | `/scheduler/` | scheduling, the **SAS Job Schedules** view |

## What's in it

**Background jobs.** *Submit as Background Job* in the Run menu under the running man, the editor context menu, and the Command Palette. The **Background Jobs** view lists your jobs from the server, newest first, so jobs from before a restart show up too. Running jobs update while the view is visible. Open a finished job's **Log**, colored from the line types SAS recorded, and its **Listing**. You can also show the submitted code, run a job again with the same values, cancel, and delete. A notification says when a job you submitted ends, including when it completed with SAS warnings.

**Saved SAS jobs.** *Save as SAS Job...* stores the whole program in My Folder or a SAS Content folder given by path, and offers the macro variables it reads but doesn't set (`&cutoff`) as parameters with defaults. The **SAS Jobs** view lists all your SAS jobs, including those made in SAS Studio. *Run...* asks for each parameter starting from its default; *Run with Defaults* doesn't ask.

**Schedules.** *Schedule...* on a SAS job, or *New Schedule...* in the **SAS Job Schedules** view. It asks for the parameter values and when to run: daily, weekdays, weekly on chosen days, monthly on a day or the last day, every few hours or minutes, once, or on several dates, in the local time zone. Each run is an ordinary background job. The view shows when each schedule runs (*Weekdays at 06:30*), and hovering shows its values, next runs, and last run. It also offers Run Now, Disable/Enable, and Delete.

**Settings:** `SAS.backgroundJobs.computeContext` (by default the profile's context, as for console runs) and `SAS.backgroundJobs.keepResultsFor` (default `P7D`; expiry deletes the job's log and listing too).

## Checked against a live SAS Viya server

Every request shape was probed against a live server before code was written. The product code was then run end to end against it in each phase (13, 9, and 10 checks), and the UI was tried in Positron after each phase. Behaviour the published specs don't mention, now handled:

- Without an `Accept-Language` header the Job Execution service passes `mul` to the Compute Server, and **every job fails** with error 5023.
- **No ODS HTML** is captured from a job, whatever the ODS form, fileref, or `_resultFilter`. A job returns its log and listing, so *Open Results* shows the listing. The ODS wrapper of console runs (`ods _all_ close;`) is not submitted, because it left jobs with no results at all.
- `logLocation` is the JSON log, `{type, line}` items in the shape the log viewer already reads.
- A job definition `PUT` must repeat the `id` and needs `If-Match` (428 without, 412 when stale). Creating a definition whose name is already in the folder fails with 400.
- A job can end `completed` with an `error` set: SAS warnings. It now shows as *Completed with warnings*.
- Cancelling, and running a stored job request, need a request body. A bodyless request through axios gets a default `Content-Type` and a 415.
- The Scheduler has no published API. Every listed hour of a trigger starts its own series. Pause/resume answers 200 but leaves no trace, so enabling sets the triggers' `active` flag. A trigger that can never fire is refused with error 11304. A schedule can only be changed by its owner.

One bug reached manual testing. An every-5-minutes schedule fired one job per elapsed hour at each mark, because the trigger listed all 24 hours. It's fixed in the last commit. As a safety net, a new schedule's next ten fire times are now checked (distinct, and evenly spaced for minute/hour intervals), and the schedule is deleted before it can run if they're wrong. The fix was proven by a real firing that ran no job.

## Commits

The first commit moves the Viya connection and the service probe from `client/src/clinical/` into a shared `client/src/viya/`. Clinical keeps its names through re-exports, and the commit changes no behaviour. The rest adds `client/src/backgroundJobs/` phase by phase, each with its docs.

Files shared with upstream are touched minimally, to keep upstream merges clean:
- `package.json`: insertions only.
- `package.nls.json`: appended keys.
- `client/src/node/extension.ts`: an import and one registration line.
- `website/docs/matrix.md` and `website/docs/Features/running.md`: one line each.

The locale files are not regenerated.

## Tests

- `npm run test-positron`: 640 passing. That includes 81 new tests for the REST models, triggers, parameters, and the fire-time check, with fixtures recorded from the live server (host and user names replaced).
- Lint clean, build and docs site (with its broken-link check) succeed.

## Not in this PR

- The listing opens as plain text. Rendering it better is deferred.
- Background jobs give the listing, not ODS HTML. That's a server limitation, and it's documented, with the console as the way to get HTML.
- Schedules can't be edited in place; delete and create a new one.

title: Release 0.7.0
Positron: coexist with Positron's own .sas7bdat/.xpt reader (#141)
description:
Fixes #141. Positron 2026.12 (posit-dev/positron#17215) opens `.sas7bdat` and `.xpt` files in its own Data Explorer without a session. This extension's viewers were registered as `default`, which outranks Positron's `builtin` editor. Positron then asked which default editor to use, and without a SAS session the extension's viewer failed with "No active SAS session".

## What it does
- **Viewers are now an option:** `sas.sas7bdatViewer` and `sas.xptViewer` are registered with `"priority": "option"`, so the "multiple default editors" prompt is gone.
- **Older Positron:** when Positron can't read the file (before 2026.12, or its reader is turned off in `dataExplorer.fileReaders`), a double-click would open binary text. The extension reopens that tab with the SAS viewer.
- **New default on 2026.12, `SAS.dataFiles.openWith: sasWhenSessionRuns`:** while a SAS session runs, a file Positron opened is reopened through SAS. `positron.dataExplorer.getContext()` gives its `fileUri`. With `positron`, Positron's viewer is kept. Positron reads the file before the swap, so `workbench.editorAssociations` is documented as the way to always use SAS.
- **Open with SAS:** a new entry on `.sas7bdat` / `.xpt` files in the Explorer context menu.
- **No session:** the SAS viewers hand the file to Positron's reader when it can read it. PROC CPORT and multi-member `.xpt` files are detected with `countTransportMembers` and excluded. Otherwise a message offers **Start SAS Session**, and the file opens once the session is up.
- **Views:** the Clinical Repository, Workspace and version history trees, job results, and SAS Content open data files with the SAS viewer explicitly.
- **Local files with a remote SAS server:** when SAS can't see the file's folder (`EXIST` / `FILEEXIST` check), the file is copied into WORK, as Clinical Repository files are. On Viya without shared storage, local files now open.

title: Positron: compare SAS datasets with PROC COMPARE
description:
Part 2 of #140: compare two SAS datasets with `PROC COMPARE`, as the Compare Data step of SAS Studio does.

Stacked on #143: merge that first. This PR's base then becomes `main`.

## What it does
- **Ways to start a comparison:**
  - **SAS: Compare Datasets...** in the Command Palette. It lists the datasets open in Data Explorers first, then lets you choose a library and a dataset.
  - **Compare with Another Dataset...** (diff icon) in the title bar of a SAS Data Explorer. The dataset in front is the base dataset, found with `positron.dataExplorer.getContext()`.
  - **Select Dataset for Compare**, **Compare Dataset with Selected** and **Compare Datasets** on `.sas7bdat` and `.xpt` files in the Explorer. Files are assigned to libraries with the helpers from #143. An `.xpt` file with several datasets asks which one to compare.
  - The compare commands of the Clinical Repository now compare two data files as datasets, not as text.
- **Options:** ID variables, picked from the variables both datasets have. Both datasets are sorted by them into `WORK._B_<mem>` / `WORK._C_<mem>` first. A numeric tolerance is optional (`METHOD=ABSOLUTE CRITERION=`).
- **Run:** the code runs in the console, so users can reuse it. The report opens in the Viewer, left-aligned with `nocenter ls=132`, and the user's options are restored afterwards.
- **Result:** a message decodes `&SYSINFO` (for example *observations only in the base dataset, unequal values*) and offers two actions:
  - **Highlight Differences** reads `WORK._COMPARE` and shows the differing observations in the Viewer as an HTML page (light and dark). Base and compare values are paired by ID, or by observation number without IDs. The values that differ are coloured (base red, compare blue, so red-green colour vision can tell them apart), observations only one dataset has are shaded, and only the variables that differ are shown. Differences are judged from the DIF rows, so the tolerance applies. The page shows at most 1,500 rows of `WORK._COMPARE`.
  - **Open Differences** opens `WORK._COMPARE` (`OUTNOEQUAL OUTBASE OUTCOMP OUTDIF`) in the Data Explorer.
  - **Open Side by Side** opens both datasets in two editor groups. It reuses the base dataset's Data Explorer if one is already open.
- **Data Explorer tab names:** a SAS Data Explorer now reports its title as `display_name`. Tabs read, for example, `Data: Differences: WORK.A vs W...` or `Data: adsl.xpt: ADSL`, instead of the library the extension assigned.
- **Posit Assistant:** the `sas-results` skill gets a "Comparing datasets" section.
- **Docs and CHANGELOG:**
  - a new docs page, `website/docs/Features/compareDatasets.md`, linked from the Positron and Clinical Acceleration pages;
  - CHANGELOG entries.

## Why the highlighting is in the Viewer
The Data Explorer can't colour cells: our backend sends values as plain strings, and Positron has no way to style them. So the side-by-side Data Explorers can't highlight differences, and **Highlight Differences** shows them in the Viewer instead.

## Testing
- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 523 passing. New tests in `compareHighlight.test.ts` (row pairing, difference rules, HTML) and `datasetCompare.test.ts` (code generation, `&SYSINFO` decoding, status parsing, common columns, tab labels), plus tests for transport files in `dataFiles.test.ts` and for `display_name` in `sasDataExplorer.test.ts`.
- Tested by hand in Positron with local SAS, comparing `WORK.A` with `WORK.B` with ID `Name`:
  - the title-bar button takes `WORK.A` as the base without asking;
  - the message names the observation only in the base dataset and the unequal values;
  - the Viewer report is readable;
  - **Open Differences** shows Alfred's BASE, COMPARE and DIF rows and Barbara's BASE row;
  - **Open Side by Side** shows two editor groups.
  - **Highlight Differences** colours Alfred's age and shades Barbara's row.

title: Positron: choose which parts of the SAS log the console shows
description:
## Summary

The SAS console shows the echoed source, notes, warnings and errors all together. This adds a filter:

- A filter button in the title bar of the **Console** pane (shown while a SAS console is in front; filled while part of the log is hidden) and **SAS: Choose Console Log Output** in the Command Palette open a multi-select quick pick: **Source**, **Notes** (NOTE lines and other log text), **Warnings**, **Errors**.
- The choice is saved in the new setting `SAS.console.logOutput` (default: all four, so the console behaves as before) and applies from the next run.
- Hidden errors and warnings are still counted, so the error summary with the Posit Assistant Fix/Explain actions and the `⚠ N warning(s)` line always appear. Editor squiggles and the Problems pane are unchanged.
- The **SAS Log** output channel keeps the full, unfiltered log.

### Multi-line messages
SSH and stdio send untyped lines, which are classified by their text. That classification moved from the session class into `consoleLog.ts` so it can be unit tested. An indented line right after an ERROR or WARNING now belongs to that message, so hiding notes doesn't cut a multi-line syntax error in half. These lines are also added to the error text passed to the assistant, but don't add to the error/warning counts. This matches the rule in `findSasErrors` (`xptFormat.ts`).

### Changes
- `client/src/positron/consoleLog.ts`: `classifyLogLine`, `logCategory`, `createLogLineClassifier`, `parseLogOutputSetting` (no `vscode` imports)
- `client/src/positron/consoleLogFilter.ts`: reads the setting; the quick-pick command. It is Positron-only, so upstream's `settings.ts` is untouched.
- `PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.ts`: `emitLogMessage` always counts errors and warnings but only streams lines in the active categories; the warning summary goes through the new `emitStream` and is never filtered.
- `package.json` / `package.nls.json`: setting, command, palette entry (`when: isPositron`, a Positron built-in context key), and `view/title` entries for `workbench.panel.positronConsole`. Positron's console action bar (Restart, Console Information, Clear) is a fixed list with no menu for extensions, so the button goes in the pane's title bar. The context keys `SAS.consoleForeground` (set from the foreground session) and `SAS.consoleLogFiltered` pick the outline or filled filter icon
- Docs: `Features/positron.md` (SAS Console) and `Configurations/sasLog.md`; CHANGELOG under **Unreleased**

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run test-positron`: 489 passing, including new tests for the classifier, categories, continuation lines and setting parsing
- [x] Lint and `tsc` clean for the changed files; VSIX packages
- [ ] In a SAS console, run `data x; set sashelp.class; run; proc print data=nope; run;`:
  - with the default filter, the output is the same as before
  - with only Errors and Warnings ticked, the ERROR lines (including continuations) and the error summary appear, and **Output › SAS Log** still has the source and notes
  - with nothing ticked, only the error summary and result note appear

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: link an authenticator app for signing
description:
Users can now link the authenticator app that **Sign Files...** needs from inside Positron. Until now, this meant going to the Settings of the SAS Clinical Acceleration Repository web app.

## What it does
- **Set Up Signing (Authenticator App)...** is in the Command Palette and in the title bar `...` menu of the Clinical Repository view.
- It first confirms with the user: a new code unlinks any app linked before.
- It then calls `POST /clinicalRepository/repository/signatureKeys` and shows the QR code it returns, so the app can scan it.
- **Sign Files...** now offers **Set Up Authenticator...** next to **Retry with a New PIN** when the server refuses a signature. After the setup, it asks for a PIN again, and the other choices are kept.

## How the request was found
The request isn't in the API documentation. It comes from the web app's JS bundle: component `F` of the Enable Signatures setting, and function `N6` of module 23730.
- It's a `POST` with no body.
- The response body is a base64 PNG, which the web app shows as `data:image/png;base64,…`.
- The web app makes no status check, so there's no way to tell whether a key exists already.
- `parseQrImage` also accepts a JSON string, an object form, or a data URL, as a guard.

## Keeping the secret safe
The QR code holds the user's TOTP secret.
- It's shown in a webview of its own (`SAS.clinical.enableSignatures`). It is **not** in the Viewer, which Posit Assistant reads, and it doesn't go through the local report server.
- The webview runs no scripts, forms or command URIs, and has no local resources.
- Its CSP is `default-src 'none'; img-src data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`.
- It has no serializer, so it isn't restored after a reload, and it isn't retained when hidden. It closes after 10 minutes.
- The image is never logged or written to disk. Parse errors don't repeat the response.
- The Assistant skill tells the model never to ask for, read or describe the code.

## Not live-verified
This request replaces the user's signing key, so it wasn't run against a server. Live check, as **demouser** on caf.pcluster (never viya_admin):
- [x] Set Up Signing shows a QR code that an authenticator app can scan.
- [x] Sign Files with a PIN from that app succeeds. This also verifies the SIGN request, which hasn't been checked yet either.
- [x] Generating again makes the old app's PINs fail. If it doesn't, update the warning in the docs and in the confirmation.

## Tests
- `clinicalSignatures.test.ts`:
  - `parseQrImage` accepts the response forms above.
  - It refuses anything else, without echoing it.
  - The page has the CSP and no scripts.
  - The page refuses an image string that could break out of the page.
- `RepositoryModel.test.ts`: the exact URL, no body, and `responseType: "text"`.
- `npm run test-positron` passes (480), and so do the RepositoryModel tests (36, plain mocha). eslint, prettier and tsc pass on the changed TypeScript files, and `npm run compile` succeeds.

Docs: the Signatures section of `website/docs/Features/clinicalAcceleration.md` gets "Link an authenticator app". The changelog has an entry.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: search the repository
description:
Phase 4, the last, of repository search, audit history and signatures. **Stacked on #132** (← #131 ← #130).

## What it adds

**Search Repository**, like the Search page of SAS Clinical Acceleration Repository. It's in the **Clinical Repository** title bar (magnifier), as **Search in This Folder...** on folders, and in the Command Palette. Four steps, which remember the last search:

1. **Name:** `like(name,…)`, with `*` and `?`, case ignored. Without a wildcard, the whole name must match, as the guide says.
2. **Location:** the selected folder, anywhere, a chosen folder, or a typed path, as `startsWith(path,'/X/')` (subfolders included). The prompt is now shared with Search Audit History (`locationPrompt.ts`).
3. **File content:** `GET /repository/files?filter=…&text=…`, with `+` and `-` escaped as the web app does. Text can't start with a wildcard.
4. **Refinements:** only files or only folders and contexts, owned by me, checked out by me, signed (`in(signingStatus,'CURRENT','BOTH')`), modified in the last 7 or 30 days.

A search with no condition at all asks for confirmation first.

**The new view:** **Clinical Repository Search**, collapsed at first, with a welcome button.
- Results (at most 500, one page) are drawn by the repository tree's `getTreeItem`, so icons, Signed and checkout markers and the `contextValue` are identical. Each result also shows its folder.
- **The repository item context menus now also apply to the search view** (23 `when` clauses widened to `(view == clinicalrepositorydataprovider || view == clinicalsearchprovider)`), plus **Reveal in Clinical Repository**. Reveal needs the new `RepositoryDataProvider.getParent`, through `GET /repository/paths?path=`.
- Commands invoked from the search view act on its selection (`selectionOf` in `index.ts`).
- Selecting a result fills Properties and Version History.
- `refreshAll` runs the search again.
- **Messages:** the count; "first N of M" when the total is larger; "content search stopped at its limit" when `limitReached`; no results; errors.

## Live-verified API facts (read-only probe as `demouser`, 2026-11-13)

- `like(name,'*.sas')` and `like(name,'tes?.sas')` match case-insensitively; **`eq(name,'test*')` returns nothing**, despite the spec's example.
- These filters are accepted: `startsWith(path,…)`, `eq(owner,…)`, `eq(checkedOutBy,…)`, `in(signingStatus,…)`, `ge(modifiedTimeStamp,<ISO>)`, `in(primaryType,…)`, `or(…)`.
- `count` of an item search is the total (102 with `limit=3`, plus a `next` link).
- `/repository/files?text=data AND run` works, and returns `limitReached` (true even with 1 result, so it's shown as "may have more").

Match any (the web app's "Match any rule") is not offered: every condition must hold.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: fixes from the live check of search, audit and signatures
description:
**Draft.** It collects the fixes the live check of #130–#133 finds. **Stacked on #133** (← #132 ← #131 ← #130). So far it has only an empty commit; each fix is added as its own commit, and its item below gets a note.

## Setup

- Install the VSIX built from `feat/clinical-repository-search` (all four phases), then **Developer: Reload Window**.
- The server is caf.pcluster, with a Viya profile. Use two accounts: `demouser` (normal user) and `viya_admin` (administrator).
- **Before signing:** in SAS Clinical Acceleration Repository, open your user **Settings → Enable Signatures → Generate a new QR code**, and scan it with an authenticator app (as `demouser`).
- Keep the **SAS Clinical Repository** output channel open. Each search logs its filter there, and each signing logs the files, role and reason, never the PIN.
- **Throwaway files:** a signature can't be removed, so sign only throwaway files. A good choice is a new versioned file, `/PositDemo/SAS-Demo/programs/livecheck.sas`.

Legend: ✅ works · ❌ fails (with a note) · ⏭ not tested

## 1. Repository search (#133)

- [ ] **Entry points:** the magnifier in the **Clinical Repository** title bar opens the 4-step wizard; so do **Search in This Folder...** on a folder, and **SAS Clinical Acceleration: Search Repository...** in the Command Palette.
- [ ] **View:** the **Clinical Repository Search** view opens and gets focus. Before any search, it shows the welcome text and a button.
- [ ] **Name:** `test*`, Anywhere, no text, no refinements finds the `test.*` files under `/PositDemo/SAS-Demo/programs`, each with its folder shown.
- [ ] **Case:** `TEST.SAS` (no wildcard, other case) finds only `test.sas`.
- [ ] **`?` wildcard:** `tes?.sas` finds `test.sas`.
- [ ] **Folder search:** **Search in This Folder...** on `/PositDemo/SAS-Demo` offers that folder first. With **Only files**, it finds only files below it.
- [ ] **Location by path:** **Enter a Path...** with `/PositLabs/` works; the trailing `/` is dropped.
- [ ] **Location by picker:** **Choose a Folder...** browses the repository and uses the chosen folder.
- [ ] **Content:** text `data` under `/PositLabs` finds only files. If the server reports `limitReached`, the message says more may match.
- [ ] **Content validation:** text `*data` is refused with a message.
- [ ] **Refinements:** **Owned by me**, **Checked out by me**, **Signed** (after section 2) and **Modified in the last 7 days** each narrow the results as expected. **Only files** plus **Only folders** together behaves like neither.
- [ ] **No conditions:** a search with no condition asks before listing up to 500 items.
- [ ] **Truncation:** a broad search (`*`, Anywhere) says "first N of M" when more than 500 match.
- [ ] **Folder results:** expand like in the repository tree.
- [ ] **Selection:** selecting a result fills **Properties** and **Version History**.
- [ ] **Context menu:** the same as in the repository for the same item, plus **Reveal in Clinical Repository**. Try **Download**, **Copy Path**, **Check out to Workspace** (needs write access) and **Show Audit History** from a result.
- [ ] **Multi-select:** with several results selected, **Download** acts on all of them, not only the clicked one.
- [ ] **Reveal:** **Reveal in Clinical Repository** expands the repository tree down to the item and selects it, also for an item several folders deep.
- [ ] **Title bar:** **Edit Search...** prefills the last answers; **Refresh Search** runs it again; **Clear Search** empties the view, and Edit, Refresh and Clear disappear.
- [ ] **Refresh after actions:** after a check-out from a result, the search results refresh too.
- [ ] **Not available:** with a non-CA profile or no CA service, the view isn't shown.

## 2. Sign Files (#131)

- [ ] **Menu:** **Sign Files...** is offered on files that aren't checked out and on folders. It isn't offered on files checked out by you or by others.
- [ ] **No privilege:** an account without the Sign Files privilege gets the privilege message before any prompt, if such an account exists.
- [ ] **Reasons and roles:** the lists match the web app (reasons Approve and Reject; the 7 roles).
- [ ] **Single file:** signing one file skips the checklist. The step titles read "Sign Files (2/4)" to "(4/4)".
- [ ] **Folder:** signing a folder shows the checklist of its files with all checked. Checked-out files are left out, and the placeholder says how many.
- [ ] **Confirmation:** the modal names the signer, reason, role and files (the first 10, then "and N more"). **Cancel** stops without a request.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: sign files
description:
Phase 2 of repository search, audit history and signatures. **Stacked on #130**: merge that first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

## What it adds

**Sign Files...** in the **Clinical Repository** context menu. It's offered on files that aren't checked out and on folders, with multi-selection; read access is enough. The flow follows the guide's Sign a File steps:

1. **Files:** a checklist, all checked, when folders or several files are selected. Folders are expanded, capped at 500 files. Checked-out files are left out and counted, because SAS refuses them.
2. **Reason:** from `GET /repository/signatureReasons`. There's no free text.
3. **Role:** from `GET /repository/signatureRoles`.
4. **Comment:** optional, with a best-practice hint.
5. **Confirmation:** a modal naming the signer, reason, role and files, and saying the signature can't be removed.
6. **PIN:** a password box for 6 to 8 digits. It comes last because a TOTP code expires within about 30 s.

Then `POST /repository/items/batch?action=SIGN&clientId=…` with `{pin, role, reason, comment, paths}`, tracked like other batch actions:
- **Failed or refused** (error, or an ERROR action status): **Retry with a New PIN** asks only for a new PIN.
- **Signed one file:** offers **Show Signature History** (#130).
- **Sign Files privilege:** checked first through `/authorizations/{id}/privileges` (`PRIVILEGE_SIGN_FILE`). If the privileges can't be read, the command goes on and the server decides, as versioning does.

## The PIN

- It's never logged, cached or stored. The output channel logs only the signer, role, reason, comment and paths; a unit test checks that the PIN isn't in that line.
- Error messages come from the server's `message`, never from the request.
- The Assistant skill says signing is the user's own act. The Assistant must never sign, or ask for or handle a PIN.

title: Positron: keep the local SAS profile when settings.json is written concurrently
description:
## Summary

Bug fix. On the first start of Positron in the SAS Analytics Pro image, the auto-added `local` profile sometimes never reached settings.json (2 of 3 runs):
- Positron showed "Failed to save 'settings.json': The content of the file is newer…".
- settings.json stayed dirty with `"SAS.connectionProfiles": {"activeProfile": "", "profiles": {}}`.
- The status bar said "No Profile". Before the console start this made the start fail; after it, Run asked for a new profile name.

**Trigger:** Posit Workbench writes `remote.autoForwardPorts` and `files.associations` to settings.json at session start when they're missing. A configuration write of the extension that overlaps it fails the file's modified-time check. Once one write fails, settings.json stays dirty and later writes are refused.

**What made the extension vulnerable:**
- **Unawaited empty writes.** The dirty content was not the profile but an empty skeleton, written unawaited:
  - `ProfileConfig.validateSettings()` wrote it on *every read* while the setting was missing, and activation reads it many times;
  - `triggerProfileUpdate()` wrote `activeProfile: ""` on every `SAS.connectionProfiles` change event, even when it was already `""`.
- **Two writes for one profile.** `addLocalSasProfile` wrote the profile and then the active profile separately.
- **No retry.** Nothing retried a failed write, and `SAS.localProfileAdded` was set regardless, so no later start tried again.

## Design

- `validateSettings()` (`components/profile.ts`, upstream file, minimal edit) only checks and never writes. Callers already treat a missing setting as no profiles, and every write sets the whole object.
- `triggerProfileUpdate()` (`node/extension.ts`) clears the active profile only when there is a stale name to clear.
- `ProfileConfig.saveProfiles(activeProfile, profiles)` writes both in one configuration update.
- `addLocalSasProfile` (`positron/localSasProfile.ts`):
  - Up to 5 attempts, waiting 1, 2, 4 and 8 s between them.
  - Each attempt re-reads the settings, stops if a stdio profile is there by now, makes one `saveProfiles` call, and succeeds only if the profile reads back.
  - Profiles another writer added meanwhile are kept, and an existing active profile stays active.
  - `SAS.localProfileAdded` is set only on success, so a failed add is retried at the next start.
  - Each failure is logged with `console.warn` to the extension host log. After the last, the injected `onFailed` callback runs. The wait and the callback are injectable, so the module stays free of `vscode`.
- **Retry warning.** Activation wires `onFailed` to a non-modal warning: "SAS could not save the local SAS profile to settings.json (…). If settings.json has unsaved changes, save or revert it, then click Retry." **Retry** runs the add again. The extension doesn't revert a dirty settings.json itself, since it may hold the user's edits.
- Activation still awaits the add before the Positron integration starts, so runtime discovery sees the profile. Only a conflict delays it, by at most about 15 s.
- The import order and line wrapping in `extension.ts` are left as on `main`: no reformatting of upstream files.

## Testing

- `localSasProfile.test.ts`: the existing cases now go through `saveProfiles`. New cases cover:
  - one write carrying both the profile and the active name;
  - success after two conflicts, with 1 s and 2 s backoff;
  - all 5 attempts failing: flag unset, `onFailed` called once;
  - a write that doesn't read back counts as failed;
  - a stdio profile appearing between attempts stops without a second write;
  - profiles added by another writer meanwhile are kept.
- 426 passing; types, lint (source files) and the build are clean. The upstream `profile.test.ts` runs in the VS Code host, in CI; no case there expects `validateSettings` to write.
- **Verified live** by the user on 2026-11-12 on their remote sas/apro system, with a VSIX of this branch.
- **How to verify live** in the sas/apro image, about 5 times, since the failure was intermittent:
  1. Delete settings.json, or leave out `remote.autoForwardPorts` and `files.associations`.
  2. Clear `SAS.localProfileAdded` (IndexedDB `positron-web-state-db-global`, key `posit.positron-sas`).
  3. Start a fresh session.
  4. Expect `local` as the active profile, no "Failed to save" notification, no empty skeleton, and the console starting with Run working. "Could not save the local SAS profile (attempt …)" lines in the extension host log show a conflict that a retry recovered from.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: show the check-in locations a .cmnf records
description:
## Summary

Bug fix. The manifest report showed **Check-in locations: None** for a repository run, although the job and the run's `.cmnf` file list `outputs/`, and the PDF there was checked in.

The rendering was fine; the data source wasn't. All three ways to open the report read the manifest from the clinical jobs service, never from the file:
- a run in the Clinical Jobs view: `/submissions/{id}/manifest`;
- a workspace `.cmnf`: the file is read only for its run id, then the same endpoint is used;
- a repository `.cmnf`: `/clinicalJobs/repository/manifests/{id}`.

The service's copy came back without the locations (`locations: []`; even the spec's example shows an empty list), while the `.cmnf` file keeps them.

## Design

- `manifestFileCheckin(text)` (`jobs/utils.ts`) reads `checkinSpecification` from `.cmnf` text. The raw `.cmnf` format differs from the API's manifest, so location entries are accepted as `{path}`, `{resource: {path}}`, `{file: {path}}`, or a plain string. Anything else is skipped.
- `withFileCheckin(manifest, fromFile)` fills in the file's locations only when the service listed none. It keeps the service's versioning settings and falls back to the file's when the service sent no check-in settings at all.
- `JobsModel.readManifestFileCheckin` reads the `.cmnf` from the workspace, or from the repository **at the version the run wrote** (`manifest.manifest.resource.fileVersion`), so an old run's report shows that run's locations. `JobsBackend` gains `getContent`/`getVersionContent`, which `RepositoryModel` already has.
- `ManifestReports.forRun` and `forFile` complete the manifest this way and log to the **SAS Clinical Repository** output channel when they do. If the file can't be read, they log a warning and the report shows what the service sent, as before.
- **Export Manifest... (JSON)** exports the completed manifest.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the parsing (all entry shapes, invalid text), the merge (fill-in, keeping the service's settings, no change when the service lists locations), and the model reading workspace, versioned and latest repository files. 420 passing; lint, types and the build are clean.
- **Not verified live:** the user's run is in another environment. The assumption that the service's manifest has empty locations while the `.cmnf` has them comes from the user's report; when the fix applies, the output channel line confirms it.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: mark test and populate runs; Run Again keeps the kind
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #123. This commit was pushed to that branch after it was merged, so it didn't reach `main`.

- **Run kinds in the Clinical Jobs view.** A test run looked exactly like a normal run; the user couldn't tell them apart. Runs other than a plain run now carry their kind in the description: **Test**, **Run and populate**, **Run and populate, relative paths**, or **Scheduled**. A test run's tooltip says what a test does: programs and inputs read from the repository, only log, listing and manifest written, nothing checked in. The progress notification of a test says "Testing … as a repository run".
- **Run Again keeps the kind.** Run Again on a test run started a *normal* run, which writes all outputs. It now repeats a run as the same kind, based on its run context: a test as a test, Run and populate as Run and populate with the same path style.

## Design

- `runKindOf(jobRunContext)` (`jobs/utils.ts`) maps the server's run context to the `RunKind` used by `JobRunner.submit`: `INTERACTIVE_TEST`, `INTERACTIVE_RUN_AND_POPULATE` and `INTERACTIVE_RUN_AND_POPULATE_RELATIVE`. Plain and scheduled runs stay plain.
- The description label is in `JobsDataProvider`. `jobRunContext` was already passed through by `normalizeSubmission`.
- Docs, the Assistant skill and the CHANGELOG entry for Test are updated.

## Testing

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: Run and Populate and Test clinical jobs
description:
## Summary

Adds **Run and Populate Clinical Job...**, as described in the SAS Clinical Acceleration guide ("Run and Populate a Clinical Job", printed pages 137–138).

A job run from the repository works in a transient workspace that holds only the files and folders in the job's Publish Setup and its file and folder parameters. A job that works in the workspace can therefore fail from the repository because its data isn't there; a user hit exactly this. Run and Populate runs a workspace job and, if the run succeeds, the service:
- replaces Publish Setup with the files the programs read and the folders they write to;
- removes the check-in locations;
- leaves programs, parameters and the description alone.

The user chooses **Use Relative Paths** (`./`, `../` from the job's folder) or **Use Absolute Paths**. A failed run leaves the job unchanged.

Where it is:
- the context menu of a `.cjob` in the **Clinical Workspace** view;
- the editor title bar menu;
- the Command Palette;
- a **Run and Populate...** button in the job editor.

Unsaved changes are saved first, as SAS Studio does. Afterwards a notification says how many files and folders Publish Setup lists, and an open job editor reloads the populated job.

**Test Clinical Job...** ("Test a Clinical Job", printed pages 135 and 144–145) runs a workspace job as if it ran from the repository, so you find out before check-in whether it will work there:
- programs and inputs are read from their repository locations;
- file and folder parameters are picked in the repository;
- only the log, listing and manifest are written, to the workspace. Nothing is checked in and no audit record is created.

A passed test can't rule out check-in problems such as missing write permission; the message says so. It sits next to Run and Populate in the same menus and has a **Test...** button in the job editor.

**Note:** the run-kind marks in the Clinical Jobs view and the Run Again fix were pushed after this PR was merged. They are in #124.

## Design

- **Request shape, found by probing caf.pcluster on 2026-11-11** (the public spec documents neither part):
  - `POST /clinicalJobs/submissions?action=RUN_AND_POPULATE` gives run context `INTERACTIVE_RUN_AND_POPULATE`, with absolute paths.
  - Adding the **body** field `"useRelativePaths": true` gives `INTERACTIVE_RUN_AND_POPULATE_RELATIVE`, with `./` paths. A query parameter of that name is silently ignored, and `RUN_AND_POPULATE_RELATIVE` is not a valid action.
  - A repository job gets 400, error 145526 ("can only be performed on clinical jobs in workspace locations"). So the command is offered for workspace jobs only, and it explains this when invoked on a repository job.
- A test run is `action=TEST` (run context `INTERACTIVE_TEST`), seen in the same probe. The probe's test failed with "Test run failed because /probe-jobs/populate_probe.sas or the specified version could not be accessed", because that program isn't in the repository. That's the expected result.
- `RunKind = "test" | PopulatePaths` selects the request. Both commands share `savedWorkspaceJob`: workspace jobs only, saved first.
- `runRequest` and `publishCounts` (`jobs/utils.ts`, no vscode import) build the request and count the Publish Setup entries. `JobsModel.submit` takes an optional `PopulatePaths`.
- The quick pick for paths tells how many Publish Setup entries and check-in locations will be replaced or removed.
- `JobRunner.follow` gets an `onEnded` hook that runs before the outcome toast, so the populate summary doesn't wait for the user to dismiss that toast.
- `WorkspaceDataProvider.notifyChanged` fires a file change so open editors of the job reload. The file system reports the server's modification time.
- Docs, the Assistant skill and the Unreleased CHANGELOG are updated. The skill also explains the transient workspace of repository runs and `&_SASWS_` paths.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the requests (actions and body field) and the counts; 413 passing. Lint, types and the build are clean.
- The two request shapes and the repository refusal were verified live with a throwaway probe job in `/probe-jobs` (not committed).
- **Run and Populate verified live** on 2026-11-11, from a VSIX of this branch on a real study job, through the UI.
- **Test Clinical Job...** verified live by the user on 2026-11-11.
- The run-kind marks and the Run Again fix moved to #124.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: show your permissions; explain refused check-ins
description:
## Summary

Two changes to the Clinical Repository, prompted by a user who couldn't tell why a file couldn't be checked out or checked in:

- **Your permissions in Properties.** **Clinical Repository Properties** now lists the permissions the server grants you on the selected file or folder, such as `READ` and `WRITE`, and your versioning privileges. A missing **Check out to Workspace** used to give no hint. In the case that prompted this, `demouser` had `READ` but not `WRITE` on a file they had checked in themselves, and SAS Studio didn't offer the check-out either.
- **Check In explains what it leaves out.** Instead of "None of the selected items can be checked in", Check In names each file and the reason:
  - a copy of a repository file (from **Copy to Workspace**) that isn't checked out to you can't replace a repository version. The message says to check the file out first, notes that **Without Content** leaves your workspace file as it is, and that a missing check-out means missing write permission.
  - a file checked out by someone else can only be checked in by them.
  - otherwise, the server didn't offer the file.

  If some files can still be checked in, they are, with a warning. Every file left out is listed in the **SAS Clinical Repository** output channel.

## Design

- `sortCheckInCandidates` (`utils.ts`, no vscode import) takes the selected workspace items, the server's check-in candidates, and the user id:
  - A candidate that is a copy of a repository file (workspace status `IN_SYNC` or `OUT_OF_SYNC`) and isn't checked out is removed from the check-in. Unchanged copies (`IN_SYNC`) are left out quietly, since there is nothing to check in.
  - Candidates checked out by someone else are removed and explained.
  - Selected files the server didn't list are explained from their own status.
  - Without a known user id, check-outs are trusted, as before.
- Properties: `RepositoryModel.getPermissionNames` reads `/clinicalRepository/authorizations/{id}/permissions` afresh, and `getPrivileges` (existing) reads the privileges. The Properties view shows the item first, then adds the access rows when both lookups return; a stale selection is ignored. Rows are left out when the server doesn't answer.
- Docs, the Assistant skill and the Unreleased CHANGELOG are updated.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the candidate sorting and the new Properties rows; 408 passing. Lint, types and build are clean.
- **Not verified live yet:**
  - which of the two paths the server takes for a not-checked-out copy: leaving it out of the candidates, or listing it. Both are handled.
  - what the permissions endpoint returns for folders, for example a separate permission for adding files.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: hide runs in the Jobs view; list only your schedules
description:
## Summary

Two follow-ups to 0.6.0, from playing with the release.

**Remove runs from the Clinical Jobs view**
- **Remove from List** on a run hides it. The view now allows multiple selection, so several runs can be removed at once.
- **Clear Finished Runs** in the view title hides every finished run, including runs on pages that aren't loaded yet. Runs still going stay listed. A notification offers **Undo**.
- **Show Hidden Runs** (eye icon) lists hidden runs marked "hidden". **Restore to List** brings one back, and **Restore All Hidden Runs** is in the **…** menu.
- **Runs are only hidden in Positron**, per server and user. The run history on the server, the audit record, stays as it is.
  - The server does allow `DELETE /submissions/{id}` (OPTIONS shows it), but deleting a run removes its record and manifest lookup for everyone, which is unwelcome in an audited setting. So it isn't used.

**Bug fix: other users' schedules**
- **The cause:** as with runs, the service returns other users' schedules too, although its documentation says it returns the current user's. So as `demouser` the view showed `michael`'s schedule and offered Run Now, Edit, Disable/Enable and Delete on it.
- **Now:** the view lists only the schedules that run as the signed-in user, like the runs list.
- **Show All Users' Schedules** lists everyone's. Each is marked "by <owner>", the view title says "All users", and other users' schedules only offer **Copy Schedule ID**.

## Design

- **`jobs/hiddenRuns.ts`** is pure, with a Memento-like store. Its state holds:
  - the run ids hidden one by one;
  - a `clearedBefore` time: finished runs that ended before it are hidden, whether or not they're loaded;
  - the `shown` exceptions, for runs restored one by one.
  
  It's saved in `globalState` under `clinicalJobs.hiddenRuns:<endpoint>|<user>` and reloaded with every refresh, so a profile switch or a different user gets its own state.
- **The Jobs view** filters on display, and keeps hidden runs in the paging offset. When a page holds only hidden runs, it fetches up to 8 more pages.
- **Schedule ownership:** `isOwnSchedule` uses `runAs`, or `createdBy` if that's missing. The context value gets `;mine;` or `;others;`, and the 8 menu entries that change schedules require `;mine;`.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 398 passing. The new tests cover:
  - hiding one by one, the clear time (a run still going is never hidden), restore, re-hide, restore all and undo;
  - state per server and user, and saving before anything is loaded;
  - schedule ownership;
  - the schedule menus offering only Copy Schedule ID on other users' schedules.
- eslint and `tsc -p client` are clean.
- Live on SAS Viya, with users `michael` and `demouser`, all checks passed:
  - [x] Remove from List (single and multiple), Clear Finished Runs with Undo, a new run staying listed
  - [x] Show Hidden Runs, Restore to List, Restore All; the state is kept after a reload and is separate per user
  - [x] `demouser` no longer sees `michael`'s schedule; Show All Users' Schedules shows it as read-only

SAS Clinical Acceleration: clinical job editor
description:
## Summary

Phase 4 of the clinical jobs plan. `.cjob` files now open in a **clinical job editor**: a form instead of JSON.

- **General**: the description.
- **Programs**: add one through the workspace picker, reorder, set an optional version (empty means latest), and open it.
- **Parameters**: name, label and type (text, masked text, number, date, file or folder), with a default editor for each type. File and folder defaults can be picked.
- **Output locations**: log, results and manifest, relative to the job, with a folder picker.
- **Repository runs**: input files and folders (`publishSetup`) and the check-in of outputs (`publishCheckin`), meaning versioning, versioning of new files and locations. These only apply when the job runs from the repository.
- **Validation as you edit**, listed above the form:
  - a job without programs, or a program without a path;
  - parameter names that aren't SAS names, or that appear twice;
  - non-numeric number defaults, and invalid date defaults.
- **Buttons**: **Run** saves and then runs the job. **Open as JSON** reopens the file in the text editor.
- **New Clinical Job...** on a **Clinical Workspace** folder creates `<name>.cjob` through the API and opens it.
- **Repository jobs and versions** open read-only, with a banner.

## Design

- **A `CustomTextEditorProvider` over the JSON text.** VS Code then provides dirty state, undo/redo, save, revert and hot exit, and **Reopen Editor With → Text Editor** shows the same document.
  - Saving writes through the existing workspace file system, the same path as editing the JSON by hand. The PATCH API isn't used, so the form does its own validation.
  - The `json` language registration from #116 is what the text editor uses.
- **`jobForm.ts`** is shared by the extension and the webview, with no `vscode` import, and is unit-tested. It handles parsing and serializing, relative paths (`./a.sas`, `../programs/a.sas`), validation, date defaults, and the message types.
- **The form keeps fields it doesn't know**, such as `useSingleOutputLocation` and `outputLocation`.
  - Text fields commit on blur or Enter, so one change is one undo step.
  - The extension skips only the single echo of the form's own edit, so undo, redo and edits made in a parallel text editor still reach the form.
- **The webview** is a React bundle, `client/src/webview/ClinicalJobEditor.tsx` plus CSS in VS Code theme variables. The only upstream change is one entry in `tools/build.mjs`. The page CSP allows only a nonce'd script.
- **Palette commands** (Run Clinical Job, Show Manifest Report, Run as Clinical Job) now also find the file of an active custom editor, through `tabGroups`.
- **A bug found in live testing:** `package.json` already had a `customEditors` list for the dataset and transport viewers. A second `customEditors` key silently replaced it, because the last duplicate JSON key wins. The editor is now in the one existing list, and a test checks for exactly one `customEditors` key with the job editor as the default for `.cjob`.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 383 passing. That includes 6 new tests: the `.cjob` round trip keeps unknown fields, empty or broken JSON, relative paths, validation, date conversion and type defaults, and the `customEditors` contribution.
- eslint and `tsc -p client` are clean.
- Live on SAS Viya with Clinical Acceleration:
  - [x] `probe.cjob` opens in the form, and **Reopen Editor With...** lists Clinical Job Editor
  - [x] **New Clinical Job...** creates `job.cjob` in the folder (the server accepts a job without programs) and opens it
  - [x] after editing in the form and saving, **Open as JSON** shows the program path still relative
- **Not verified:** the shape of `publishSetup` and `publishCheckin` paths. They're stored as absolute repository paths, but the API documentation doesn't say which form the server expects.

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: link files in manifest reports; open .cjob and .cmnf as JSON
description:
## Summary

- **Links in the manifest report:** the paths of the job, programs, inputs, outputs, logs, results and the manifest file are links that open the file in Positron. A versioned repository file opens at the version the run used, through the existing `sasClinicalVersion` file system. Exported reports keep plain paths.
- **JSON for job files:** `.cjob` and `.cmnf` files are registered with the built-in `json` language. Both are strict JSON on disk, so they now get highlighting, folding and **Format Document**.

## Design

A report in the Viewer can't call the extension. It also has to stay a URL or file preview, because Posit Assistant can't read webview panels.

- **New `ViewerServer`** (`client/src/positron/viewerServer.ts`), with no `vscode` import:
  - an HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`, on a random port, started lazily;
  - every path starts with a random 128-bit token;
  - pages are kept in memory, the newest 10;
  - pages are served with `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:`, so no scripts, plus `nosniff`, `no-store` and `no-referrer`.
- **Opening the report:** `showUrlInViewer` opens the page with `previewUrl(env.asExternalUri(url))`. It activates the proxy first, and falls back if the panel isn't visible within 10 s, like `showHtmlInViewer`.
- **Clicking a link:** the href is relative to the page, `../open?target=<uri>`, so it also works behind Workbench's port forwarding. The server passes the URI to the extension and answers **204 No Content**, so the report stays in place.
  - The extension opens only `sasClinical`, `sasClinicalWorkspace` and `sasClinicalVersion` URIs. Anything else gets a 400 and a log line.
- **Fallback:** if the server or `previewUrl` fails, the previous file-based report is shown, without links.
- **Renderer:** `renderManifestReport` takes an optional `linkFor(resource)`, and escapes every href.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 377 passing. The new tests cover:
  - real HTTP round trips to `ViewerServer`: pages behind the token, a 404 without it, 204 for accepted link targets, 400 for refused or missing ones;
  - the CSP header, page pruning, and the method check;
  - report links, including escaping, and plain paths when no `linkFor` is given.
- eslint and `tsc -p client` are clean.
- Live in Positron desktop with SAS Viya and Clinical Acceleration:
  - [x] paths in the report are links; clicking the log, the program or the `.cjob` opens it in the editor, and the report stays in place
  - [ ] `.cjob` and `.cmnf` open with JSON highlighting
  - [ ] the links through Workbench port forwarding (not tested yet)

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: run a workspace program as a clinical job
description:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the clinical jobs plan, after #113 and #114.

**Run as Clinical Job** runs a `.sas` program in the **Clinical Workspace** as a clinical job, so the run gets a manifest, which is its audit record. It appears:

- in the program's context menu in the **Clinical Workspace** view;
- in the editor's **Run** menu (`editor/title/run`) and context menu, for workspace `.sas` files.

How it works:

- The first run creates `<program>.cjob` next to the program, then runs it. Later runs reuse that job, and prompt for its parameters if it has any.
- Unsaved editor changes are saved first, because the job runs the file on the server.
- If `<program>.cjob` exists and runs other programs, a dialog offers two choices:
  - **Create New Job** uses the first name, `-2`, `-3` and so on, that is free or already runs this program;
  - **Replace** updates the existing job to run only this program, with no parameters.

## Design

- **The pure helpers** `jobPathForProgram`, `runsOnlyProgram` and `programJob` are in `jobs/utils.ts` and unit-tested. `runsOnlyProgram` resolves the job's relative paths, for example `./hello.sas`, against the job's folder.
- **`ProgramJobs`** finds, creates or replaces the job, then hands it to the existing `JobRunner`.
  - It reads `<name>.cjob` from the workspace.
  - A 404 means the name is free. A file that isn't JSON is treated as "exists, not ours".
- **Workspace only.** A workspace job can only run workspace programs. The docs explain how to get a run recorded in the repository: check the job in, then run it from the Repository view.
- **The menus** use the `;sasProgram;` context token, plus `resourceScheme == sasClinicalWorkspace` in the editor menus.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 372 passing. That includes the helpers and the menu `when` clauses: the command shows on workspace programs only, and only when the jobs service is available.
- eslint and `tsc -p client` are clean.
- Live on SAS Viya with Clinical Acceleration:
  - [x] the first run creates `hello.cjob`, with no prompts, and runs it
  - [x] from the editor, unsaved changes are saved first and the existing job is reused
  - [x] an existing `slow.cjob` that runs `slow.sas` is reused
  - [x] the name conflict offers Create New Job (`-2`) or Replace
  - [x] the command does not appear on repository programs

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: show and export clinical job manifest reports
description:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the clinical jobs plan. It builds on #113.

- **Show Manifest Report** shows the manifest of a clinical job run as one HTML page in the Viewer, where Posit Assistant can read it. The manifest is the audit record of the run. The page shows:
  - the job, how the run ended, who ran it and when, the run-as user and the total time;
  - the parameter values (masked values stay hidden);
  - the programs, with result and run time;
  - each input and output, with version, size, modification time, MD5 and the program that used it, plus external references;
  - logs and results;
  - for repository jobs, the check-in settings and the outputs that failed to check in;
  - file transfer metrics.
- **Where to find it:**
  - on finished runs in the **Clinical Jobs** view, as an inline icon and in the context menu;
  - on `.cmnf` files in the **Clinical Workspace** and **Clinical Repository** views;
  - in the editor title of an open `.cmnf` file;
  - as a **Show Manifest** button in the end-of-run notification.
- **Export Manifest...** saves the report as `.html`, or the manifest as `.json`.

## Design

- **`renderManifestReport`** (`jobs/manifestReport.ts`) is pure, so it's unit-tested. It returns self-contained HTML with inline CSS, a light and a dark scheme, and print styles. Every value from the server is escaped.
- **A workspace `.cmnf`** is read for its run id, and the manifest is then fetched through `/submissions/{id}/manifest`. A repository `.cmnf` uses `/repository/manifests/{id}`. Check-in failures come from the submission.
- **New Viewer helper** `positron/viewer.ts`, moved out of `PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.emitViewerOutput`. The console session and the report share it.
  - **Bug found in live testing:** in a freshly opened window, `previewHtml` failed inside Positron with "command `positronProxy.startHtmlProxyServer` not found". The Viewer then stayed empty, and the extension saw no error.
  - **The fix:** the helper activates `positron.positron-proxy` first. If the panel is still not visible after 10 s, it disposes the panel and falls back to a preview webview.
  - Console HTML output benefits too, so this has a Bug Fixes entry in the CHANGELOG.
- **`OutputFiles.write` takes a file name**, so reports are named `manifest-<job>-N.html` instead of `sas-output-N.html`.
- **Better logging:** when the Jobs view can't load a run's manifest, the log now records the run id, HTTP status and SAS error code.
- **Docs note:** the server only returns a run's manifest while its `.cmnf` is unchanged, and the next run of the same job overwrites that file. The docs therefore suggest exporting the reports you need to keep.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 368 passing. That includes 5 new tests:
  - report rendering for a workspace run, a repository run with check-in failures, and a canceled run, including HTML escaping;
  - file names from `OutputFiles`;
  - the `.cmnf` menu `when` clauses.
- eslint and `tsc -p client` are clean.
- Live on SAS Viya with Clinical Acceleration:
  - [x] Show Manifest Report from the Clinical Jobs view opens the report in the Viewer
  - [x] the Show Manifest button in the end-of-run notification
  - [x] a canceled run is reported as canceled
  - [x] the Viewer fallback, after the proxy race above was reproduced and fixed

title: SAS Clinical Acceleration: run clinical jobs and review their runs
description:
## Summary

Adds support for **SAS Clinical Job Management** (`/clinicalJobs`), the part of SAS Clinical Acceleration that runs SAS programs with an audit record. A clinical job is a `.cjob` file that lists programs and parameters. Each run writes a manifest (`.cmnf`) that records what ran, the parameter values, and every input and output file with its version and checksum.

This covers Phases 0 and 1 of the clinical jobs plan (API client and detection; running and reviewing jobs).

- **Run Clinical Job**: in the context menu of `.cjob` files in the **Clinical Workspace** and **Clinical Repository** views, and in the editor title bar.
  - It prompts for each parameter, pre-filled with its default. Text and number parameters use an input box, masked ones a password box, dates are validated, and files and folders are picked from the job's view.
  - A notification follows the run. Its **Cancel** cancels the run on the server.
  - When the run ends, a notification offers **Open Log** and **Open Results**. Check-in failures are listed in the output channel.
- **Clinical Jobs view**: the signed-in user's runs, newest first, with live state. Runs that are still going are re-checked every 5 s while the view is visible, and older runs load page by page.
  - Expanding a run shows its manifest: Programs (execution state and time), Parameters, Inputs, Outputs, Logs, Results, and Check-in failures.
  - Files open through the existing file systems. A versioned repository file opens at the exact version the run used.
  - Run actions: **Open Log**, **Open Results**, **Open Job**, **Run Again** (same values, no prompts), **Cancel Run**, **Copy Run ID**.
- **Detection**: the service is detected separately, and sets `SAS.clinical.jobsAvailable`. The view appears only when both services are present.

## Design

- **New code** is in `client/src/clinical/jobs/`. `JobsModel` reuses the Clinical Repository's connection, so it gets the same sign-in and 401 retry.
- **Pure logic is unit-tested without VS Code**: state mapping, submission normalizing, `.cjob`/`.cmnf` parsing, parameter values and manifest grouping.
- **`ClinicalAvailability` is parameterized** by a service probe. The root `/clinicalJobs/` answers 404, so the probe asks for one submission instead.
- **`pollUntil`** is a generic poller. `pollActionStatus` is rebuilt on it, with the same behavior.
- **New context tokens** `;job;`, `;manifest;` and `;sasProgram;` drive the menus, which keeps the menu `when`-clause test effective.
- **The spec is wrong in places.** These request shapes were checked against a live server, and the code follows the server:
  - Starting a run needs `POST /submissions?action=RUN`, and the body may contain only `job` and `parameterValues`. A `version` field is rejected.
  - Text parameter values and defaults are plain strings, not `{value}`.
  - `/submissions/{id}/state` accepts only `application/json`.
  - Cancel is `PUT /submissions/{id}/state?value=canceled`, lowercase.
  - Submissions use flat `job*` fields. The types accept both that and the spec's nested form.
  - The submissions list also returns other users' runs, so it is filtered to the signed-in user.
  - Workspace jobs have no GET endpoint, so the `.cjob` JSON is read directly. A workspace `.cmnf` names its run, whose manifest is then fetched by id.
- **Log highlighting**: no custom highlighter. Positron's built-in `log` language already highlights `.log` files from the CA file systems in every theme.
- **Upstream files touched**: none.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 363 passing, including 31 new clinical job tests. They use responses recorded from the live server, with user names replaced. The compiled run from `client/out` passes too.
- eslint and `tsc -p client` are clean.
- Live on a SAS Viya server with Clinical Acceleration (workspace jobs), all checks passed:
  - [x] the Clinical Jobs view lists only my runs
