title: fix: keep idle Viya compute sessions alive and restart them when dropped
description:
## Problem

An idle SAS console on a Viya (REST) connection stopped working: the server ends a compute session that gets no requests for its inactivity timeout, and the next submit failed with a 404. Nothing in the REST path touched an idle session, and nothing recovered after it was gone. (SSH already sends keepalives.)

## Change

- **Heartbeat.** Ping an idle session every 60 seconds (`SAS.session.keepAliveSeconds`, `0` turns it off). It skips pings while a job is running and stops after 8 hours without a submit. On a 401 it refreshes the token silently and retries once; it does not call `getSession` on every tick, because that path hits the network and can sign the user out when a refresh fails.
- **Restart.** If the server drops the session anyway, the next submit starts a new one and says so in the log (the WORK library and macro variables of the old session are gone). It retries only when the 404 happens before the job was submitted, so code never runs twice.
- **Layout.** The heartbeat is in `rest/keepAlive.ts` with no `vscode` imports, so it is unit-tested with fake timers (14 tests in `client/test/positron/keepAlive.test.ts`). The `RestSession` changes are additive: the old `_run` body is now `_runOnce`, wrapped by the restart logic, so the shared file has no re-indentation.

## What was verified against a real Viya server

Probed with a temporary debug command (not in this PR):

- Both `GET .../state` and `GET .../sessions/{id}` reset the inactivity timer. Sessions polled every ~5s survived about four times a 30s timeout while an unpolled control died.
- `attributes.sessionInactiveTimeout` is accepted, but its unit appears to be **seconds**, and small values ended sessions within seconds. This PR deliberately does not send it.

End to end in Positron:

- A console idle for 10+ minutes still responded on return.
- After the compute session pod was terminated, the next submit showed the restart warning and then ran normally in a new session.

## Not verified

- The server's default inactivity timeout (the context attributes are empty) and any absolute maximum session lifetime. The fixed 60s interval does not depend on either.
- Laptop sleep suspends timers, so a session can still expire while the machine sleeps; the restart path is the fallback there.
- The `RestSession` wiring has no unit tests (it needs the `vscode` API); it was exercised manually as described above.

## Notes

- No version bump; the changelog entry is under Unreleased.
- CI: `format:check` and `tsc -p ./client` are non-blocking on this repo; eslint and `tsc` report nothing in the changed files.

title: CI: skip the Translation Check in the fork
description:
## Summary

The **Translation Check** workflow has failed on every push to `main` since 2026-10-18, the merge of upstream v1.21.0 (#52). This skips it in the fork (it shows as *skipped*, not *failed*) and keeps it for upstream and for manual runs.

## Design

- **What the check does:** it runs `npm run locale --update-locales` (export the `l10n.t()` strings, merge missing keys into each locale file as English placeholders, drop unused keys, sort) and fails if `git diff` shows a change in `*.nls.*` or `l10n/*`. It says "these strings still need translating".
- **Not caused by our PRs:** it failed identically on #100 and #102, which touched no strings. It was green before #52.
- **Upstream is red too:** `sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension` runs the identical workflow and all of its last 40 runs failed. It is a signal for SAS's localization team, not a gate.
- **Why not fix the files:** every `package.nls.<locale>.json` lacks 29 of the 123 keys (upstream's Workbench and audit settings, our `clinical.*` commands, `SAS.localSasPaths`), and `package.nls.json` is not sorted, so the script would rewrite it. Regenerating the 21 locale files adds English placeholders (a missing key already falls back to English), conflicts with every upstream sync that updates translations, and is red again after the next PR that adds a string. The fork has no translators.
- **The change:** a job-level `if: github.repository == 'sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` plus a comment. The triggers are unchanged, so the diff against upstream is four lines, and **Actions > Translation Check > Run workflow** still works.

## Testing

- The YAML parses and `prettier --check` passes.
- The Translation Check does not run on pull requests. After the merge, the push to `main` should show it as *skipped*: `gh run list --repo posit-dev/positron-sas-extension --workflow translations.yml --limit 1`.

## Heads-up for the next upstream sync

Upstream merged #2152 (track `l10n/bundle.l10n.json`) and #2154 (`l10n:export`, `l10n:check`, and an `l10n:check` step in `pr.yml`) on 2026-11-03. Neither is in the fork yet. After we merge upstream, `pr.yml` will compare the committed bundle with the strings generated from `client/src`. Our Clinical Acceleration and Positron strings are not in it, so the first PR after the sync will fail until the bundle is regenerated with `npm run l10n:export` and committed. That decision belongs to the sync.

title: Fix: replay a 401 request with the refreshed token (Clinical Repository)
description:
## Summary

The Clinical Repository connection (`client/src/clinical/RepositoryModel.ts`, ported from SAS's Clinical Acceleration extension) installs a response interceptor that, on a 401, calls `updateAccessToken()` and then replays the failed request with `connection(originalRequest)`.

`updateAccessToken()` only updates `connection.defaults.headers.common.Authorization`. The failed request (`error.config`) already holds the old `Authorization` header, and request-level headers take precedence over the defaults, so the replay is sent with the old token and fails with a second 401. Only later requests, which pick up the refreshed default, succeed. In practice: after the access token expires, the first Clinical Repository action fails with a 401 even though the refresh worked, and trying again succeeds.

This sets the refreshed `Authorization` header on the replayed request before retrying.

The same bug was found in the Clinical Acceleration extension this code was ported from and is fixed there in sassoftware/vscode-sas-ca-extension#6.

Not changed: `client/src/connection/rest/RestContentAdapter.ts` has the same replay pattern, but that code comes from the SAS Extension for VS Code, so I left it alone.

## Testing

- New unit test in `client/test/clinical/RepositoryModel.test.ts`: it captures the interceptor the model installs, feeds it a 401 for a request that carries the stale token, and checks the replayed request carries the refreshed one. It fails without the fix (`expected 'Bearer token-1' to equal 'Bearer token-2'`) and passes with it.
- Ran all 15 tests in that file locally with mocha, using a scratch `vscode` mock that adds `authentication` (not part of this PR), because that suite normally runs in a VS Code host. All passed. I did not run `npm run test-client` itself, so CI is the first run in the real host.
- Reproduced the underlying behaviour against a local HTTP server that only accepts the new token, with axios 1.21.0 (the locked version): unpatched, the first request returns 401 and the second 200; with the change the first request returns 200.
- `tsc -p ./client`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` are clean on the changed files, and `copyright:check` passes.
- Not reproduced against a live SAS Viya server with a real expired token.

title: Clinical Acceleration: add the Workspace, check in, versioning, and compare
description:
## Summary

Brings the features of SAS's [Clinical Acceleration extension](https://github.com/sassoftware/vscode-sas-ca-extension) (1.0.2) into `client/src/clinical`, besides the read-only Repository view that was there (#60, #67, #69, #70). The Repository, Workspace, Properties and Version History views now cover what the SAS extension offers, with Positron specific additions (Data Explorer, Posit Assistant skill).

| | SAS CA extension | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository browse, open, rename, new folder, upload, download, check out | yes | yes | yes |
| Repository delete (soft) | yes | no | yes |
| Enable and disable versioning | yes | no | yes |
| Version History view (open, download, compare, copy to workspace) | yes | no | yes |
| Properties view | yes | no | yes |
| Compare (repository, versions, workspace) | yes | no | yes |
| Workspace view with editing, new, rename, delete, upload, download | yes | no | yes |
| Copy to Workspace (latest, folder, folder structure, one version) | yes | no | yes |
| Check in, Undo Check out | yes | partial (undo from repository) | yes |

Also fixes #73 (upload sends `multipart/form-data` and no longer versions by default).

## Design

- **`WorkspaceModel`** sits on the connection and sign-in of `RepositoryModel` (`getConnection` is now public). **`WorkspaceDataProvider`** is the tree and a *writable* `FileSystemProvider` (`sasClinicalWorkspace:/<path>`). `writeFile` awaits the server instead of upstream's fire-and-forget debounce, so a failed save reaches the user. **`WorkspaceActions`** holds the prompts and progress of the commands.
- **Batch actions** share `performBatchAction` (`batchAction.ts`). `RepositoryModel.runBatchAction` is now `startBatchAction` + `waitForAction`, because upload and download send the content between starting and polling.
- **Check in** is pure and unit tested: `planCheckIn` sorts the candidates into new, versioned and unversioned files, `getNextVersion` raises Major or Minor, and `buildCheckInBody` builds the request. The prompts around it are thin.
- **Versioning privileges** are checked when Enable/Disable Versioning runs, not per tree item (that would double the requests of every listing). They fail open: the command stops only if the server says the user holds neither privilege.
- **Menus** are driven by context values (`;file;`, `;versioned;`, `;canDelete;`, `;canCheckIn;`, ...). The tests evaluate the real `when` clauses of `package.json` against them.
- **Not copied from upstream, on purpose:** its pagination (re-requests one URL, we follow `next` links), `closeFileIfOpen` (async predicate in `Array.find`), `process.env.HOME`, and the debounced save. Version tooltips load on hover (`resolveTreeItem`) instead of one request per version.
- **Run:** `.sas` files already get the `sas` language id for any scheme, so Run works on workspace files. I left the Run `when` clauses alone: nine of those lines belong to upstream. The Data Explorer already handles non-`file` schemes. A *version* of a dataset does not open there (`adsl-v2.0.sas7bdat` is not a valid member name); that is in the docs.
- **Delete** is blocked for every context (organizations and studies). Upstream blocks only top-level ones. Say so if studies should be deletable.
- `package.json` and `package.nls.json` are purely additive (no existing line changes).
- Docs: new page "SAS Clinical Acceleration", README and docs home corrected, and a new Posit Assistant skill (`sas-clinical-acceleration`).

## Testing

- `npm run test-positron` (304 tests), the model tests in `client/test/clinical` (49, they run on CI in `test-client`), lint, `prettier --check` on the files added or changed, `copyright:check`, `npm run compile`, and a docs site build. No type errors in `client/src/clinical`.
- **Not verified against a server.** I have no CA account with write access, and the OAuth password grant is rejected for the public clients on the test cluster, so none of this ran in Positron. The requests follow the upstream extension and the unit tests pin their shape. Please test with a build of this branch:
  1. Workspace listing and opening a file (the read paths).
  2. Edit and save a workspace file.
  3. Check in a new, an unversioned and a versioned file.
  4. Rename a workspace file (the body is a JSON string) and create a folder (URL shape).
  5. Upload and expand a zip into the workspace root (`path=/` is sent).
  6. Delete, Enable Versioning and Disable Versioning in the repository.
- The CHANGELOG says which entries are not yet verified against a server with write access.

title: CI: publish a development build as a pre-release for every push to main
description:
## Summary

Every push to `main` builds the VSIX and publishes it as a numbered GitHub pre-release, so changes can be tested before the next release. This is the process of [positron-nextflow-extension](https://github.com/sol-eng/positron-nextflow-extension) (`.github/workflows/prerelease.yml`), adapted to this repo's release flow. Testers install the VSIX with **Extensions: Install from VSIX...**.

## Design

- **Trigger:** `push` to `main`, and `workflow_dispatch` to build a branch by hand (the workflow file has to be on `main` first, so this works for branches created after the merge).
- **Naming:** `main` carries the version of the *last release*, because a `package.json` version bump on `main` releases it (`package.yml`). Nextflow bumps to the next version right after a release, which would release immediately here. So a build is named after the last release: tag `v0.5.1-dev.<run number>`, title `Positron SAS 0.5.1-dev.<n> (<sha>)`, file `positron-sas-0.5.1-dev.<n>.vsix`. The VSIX inside keeps the `package.json` version, so nothing about the extension manifest changes. Positron shows the same version for a dev build and the release before it.
- **Releases are skipped:** a first `check` job compares the `package.json` version of the pushed commit with `github.event.before`. A changed version is a release, published by `package.yml`, so no dev build is made for it. (`package-json-versioned-action` compares the version in the commit with the previous commit and ignores tags, so dev tags cannot confuse it.)
- **Notes:** the `## Unreleased` section of `CHANGELOG.md` (`tools/changelog-section.mjs Unreleased`), then the non-merge commits since the last release.
- **Retention:** the five newest `-dev.N` pre-releases stay. Only tags that match `-dev.<n>` are pruned, because this repo already has an older pre-release (`v1.19.2-positron.1`) that has to stay. I tested the `jq` filter against fake data and against the real release list.
- **Tests before publishing:** `test-server` and `test-positron`, with the same environment as `pr.yml`. Actions are pinned by SHA, as in the nextflow workflow.
- **Docs:** a short "Install a development build" section on the installation page.

## Testing

- The workflow YAML parses, and `prettier --check` passes for both files.
- The version-change check, the notes generation and the retention filter were run locally against the real repository state (read-only).
- The workflow itself cannot run before it is on `main`. The first push to `main` after the merge builds the first dev build, which is the real test. Look at **Actions > Pre-release** and the **Releases** page afterwards.

title: Update dependencies (monthly group, without TypeScript 7 and KaTeX 0.19)
description:
## Summary

Replaces #86. Takes all of its updates except two that cannot be installed:

- **typescript 7.0** (the native compiler) is outside the `typescript` peer range of `@typescript-eslint/*` 8.72, so `npm install` fails with `ERESOLVE`. This is why both CI jobs failed on #86. TypeScript stays on 6.0.
- **katex 0.19**: `marked-katex-extension` 5.1.13 needs `katex >=0.16 <0.19`. KaTeX stays on 0.17.

`.github/dependabot.yml` now ignores TypeScript major updates and KaTeX 0.19 and later, with a comment on each, so the monthly group stays installable. Remove the entries once typescript-eslint and marked-katex-extension support them.

Major updates included: mocha 12, sinon 22 (`@types/sinon` 22), glob 14, `vscode-languageclient` 11, `vscode-languageserver` 11.

## Testing

Locally (macOS, Node 24):

- `npm run compile`, `npm run lint`
- `npm run test-positron`: 259 passing
- `npm run test-client` (VS Code host): 524 passing, 1 pending
- `npm run test-server` with `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true`: 17 passing. Without it, the run fails locally on `main` too, with a missing `@types/node` type in a server test, so CI is the reference here.

title: SAS Viya: sign in with the Posit Workbench OAuth token
description:
## Summary

In a Posit Workbench session, a SAS Viya (`rest`) profile now signs in with the SAS Viya OAuth token that Workbench already manages for the user through a custom OAuth integration. Users who signed in to the integration on the Workbench homepage (Managed Credentials) no longer sign in to SAS Viya a second time. Outside Workbench, or without a matching integration, the existing SAS Logon sign-in runs unchanged.

## Design

- New profile settings on Viya profiles (TypeScript type, `package.json` schema, `package.nls.json`):
  - `authentication`: `"auto"` (default), `"workbench"`, or `"sasLogon"`
  - `workbenchIntegration`: optional integration GUID
- New `client/src/connection/rest/workbenchAuth.ts`. It has no runtime `vscode` import, so it is unit tested directly.
  - Detection: an RPC cookie from `$PWB_SESSION_RUNTIME_DIR/rpc_cookie`, which is re-read on every call because Workbench rotates it, or else from `RS_SESSION_RPC_COOKIE`. Plus a target: `RS_SERVER_ADDRESS`, or else the unix socket `RS_SERVER_RPC_SOCKET_PATH` (default `/run/rstudio-server/rstudio-rserver/session-server-rpc.socket`).
  - `rpc()`: `POST <address><method>` with body `{"method", "kwparams"}` and header `X-RS-Session-Server-RPC-Cookie`. It requires HTTP 200 and an `application/json` response, like `src/go/rpc/rpc.go`. Requests skip any proxy.
  - `listIntegrations()`: flattens `providers[].integrations[]` from `/oauth_integrations`.
  - `getToken(uuid, {force})`: `/oauth_token` with `{uuid, force_refresh}`. `result:false` means no token, and `error` throws.
  - `findIntegration()`: an explicit GUID wins (case-insensitive). Otherwise it picks the single integration whose `token_url` equals `new URL("/SASLogon/oauth/token", endpoint)`, after normalizing scheme, host case, default port and trailing slash. Zero or several matches give no match.
  - `resolveWorkbenchAuth()`: decides the mode.
    - `auto`: uses a matching, authenticated integration. A matching integration the user is not signed in to gives `signInRequired`. Anything else falls back to SAS Logon silently, with a log line.
    - `workbench`: the same cases end in explicit errors (not in Workbench, RPC failed, no integration, ambiguous, GUID not found, sign-in required).
    - An expired token is force refreshed once. Workbench can return the old token when its own refresh fails.
  - `redact()`: removes known secrets, `Bearer …`, `access_token`/`refresh_token`/`id_token`/`rpc_cookie` fields and JWTs from log text. Tokens and cookies are never logged.
- `SASAuthProvider` (all `authentication.getSession("SAS")` callers keep working):
  - `getSessions`/`createSession` ask Workbench first, unless the mode is `sasLogon`. The Workbench session is in memory only and never written to SecretStorage. The account label comes from the existing `@currentUser` call.
  - If SAS Viya answers 401, the provider force refreshes once. The existing 401 handlers (RestContentAdapter interceptor, RestServerAdapter reconnect) call `getSession` again, so they pick this up.
  - A timer fetches a new token 5 minutes before `expiry`. Workbench refreshes within 6 minutes of expiry. If the global `apiConfig.accessToken` still holds the old token, the timer updates it, and it fires `onDidChangeSessions`.
  - `auto` with a matching integration the user has not signed in to: a warning asks the user to sign in to it in Posit Workbench (Managed Credentials). It offers **Try Again** and **Use SAS Logon**. The SAS Logon choice lasts for the window.
  - Sign Out forgets the Workbench token for that profile and does not revoke it. Signing in again uses it without a prompt.
- Docs: `website/docs/Configurations/Profiles/viya.md` (new "Sign In with Posit Workbench" section) and a CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` Features entry.

## Testing

- `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 243 passing. The new `client/test/positron/workbenchAuth.test.ts` runs against a real local HTTP server and a unix-socket server and covers:
  - the detection matrix
  - cookie file priority and re-reading after rotation
  - request method, path, header and body
  - success, `result:false`, `error`, expired/force refresh, non-200, non-JSON and invalid JSON responses
  - integration matching: exact, trailing slash, case, default port, other port/host/scheme, explicit GUID, zero or several matches
  - `auto`/`workbench`/`sasLogon` decisions
  - redaction, including that a cookie does not leak in connection errors
- `npm run lint`, `npm run compile`, `npx tsc -p ./client` (no errors), `prettier --check` on the changed files, `npm run copyright:check`: all clean.
- No unit tests for `SASAuthProvider` itself, because it depends on the vscode API.

## Needs live verification

- [ ] The RPC environment is visible in the Positron extension host in a Workbench session: `PWB_SESSION_RUNTIME_DIR` (or `RS_SESSION_RPC_COOKIE`) and `RS_SERVER_ADDRESS` (or the RPC socket).
- [ ] SAS Viya compute accepts the token Workbench gets from the integration. Decode the JWT and check `aud`, `scope` and `client_id` (the scopes the integration requests matter). Then start a compute session and run code.
- [ ] Integrations `/oauth_integrations` reports with `"authenticated": false` show the sign-in warning, and Use SAS Logon works.
- [ ] A long-running session keeps working across a token refresh (short token lifetime in SASLogon for the test client).
- [ ] SAS Content, which uses the RestContentAdapter axios header, works with the Workbench token.

title: Interrupt on SSH/stdio, saspy HTTP export for SAS Viya, and cleanups
description:
Three small fixes and a set of cleanups, one commit per issue.

## Interrupt on SSH and stdio (#90)

Only rest and itc sessions can cancel a submission. For SSH and stdio, `interrupt()` set the console to Idle while SAS kept running.

- The state now stays Busy until the run finishes. A warning says that this connection type cannot interrupt running code and offers **Restart Session**, which ends SAS.
- Why not a signal: the extension starts SAS with `-nodms -noterminal`. SAS answers SIGINT with an interactive attention menu (saspy's STDIO access method scrapes that menu and only supports it locally, not over SSH). Answering it from the extension is fragile, and the result is not testable without a terminal. Over SSH, `stream.signal('INT')` would reach the remote shell rather than SAS. Ending the SAS process is the only reliable way to stop it.
- stdio `_close()` kept the process attached until it exited. A restart right afterwards reused the exiting process and its closed stdin, so the new session hung. Now close detaches at once and kills the old process after the existing 1 s grace period, and the next setup spawns a new SAS.
- Docs: "Interrupting Running Code" sections in `sas9stdio.md` and `sas9ssh.md`, plus a note on the cancel row of the matrix.

## saspy export for SAS Viya (#91)

`sas_export_saspy_config` now writes saspy's HTTP access method for SAS Viya profiles: `url`, `context` (falling back to the default compute context), and `'authtoken': os.environ.get('SAS_VIYA_TOKEN')`. A comment explains how to get a token (the SAS Viya CLI, `sas-viya auth login`) and says never to put secrets in the file. Without a token, saspy prompts for a user ID and password. The generator moved to `saspyConfig.ts` so it can be unit-tested. It also quotes values for Python and turns profile names into Python identifiers.

## Cleanups (#92)

- Removed the `SAS.viewDataInPositron` command: it was declared, but nothing registered it or used it in a menu.
- `.sas7bdat` / `.xpt` custom editors: outside Positron, they reopen the file in VS Code's default editor (`vscode.openWith(uri, "default")`) and say why once per window. Before, plain VS Code showed a viewer that could only report "No active SAS session". The contribution has to stay `priority: default`, because the priority cannot depend on the host.
- stdio sessions now run the profile's `autoExec` lines once, after SAS starts. It was cheap to implement, so the documented example is now correct.
- `package.json` `repository`/`bugs` now point to posit-dev/positron-sas-extension.
- stdio README: the actual startup options and `doc/profileExamples/stdio.json`.
- Docs: `additional.md` uses `saspath`, puts stdio `sasOptions` values in separate items, and lists stdio in the autoexec section. `matrix.md` gets a SAS 9.4 (local - stdio) column, and the flowchart gets a stdio branch.

## Tests

- New `client/test/positron/interrupt.test.ts` and `saspyConfig.test.ts`.
- `client/test/connection/stdio/index.test.ts`: autoExec lines are written after startup, and close followed by setup spawns a new process and kills the old one.
- Local: lint, compile, `tsc -p ./client`, `test-positron` (205 passing), copyright check, and prettier on changed files. I also ran the stdio connection tests locally under mocha with a stub vscode module (10 passing). `test-client` itself runs in CI.

Fixes #90
Fixes #91
Fixes #92

title: Positron: start the picked profile and give each SAS console its own session
description:
## Summary

- Starting the runtime "SAS (X)" now connects with profile X. Before, the console session was built from the active profile (`getSession()` in `connection/index.ts`), so "SAS (X)" connected to Y when Y was active (#88).
- Each Positron SAS console now owns its own SAS session. Before, `stdio`, `ssh`, `rest` (and COM/IOM) kept one module-level session per connection type, so two consoles shared one SAS process or compute session, and shutting one down closed it for the other (#89).

## Design

- `connection/index.ts`: new `createSessionForProfile(name)` returns a **new** session for the named profile, using new `createSession(config)` factories in `stdio`, `ssh`, `rest` and `itc`. The existing `getSession()` (active profile, shared singleton) is unchanged, so `SAS.run*`, the Library and Content navigators, notebooks, the status bar and `SAS.close` keep their current behavior in VS Code.
- `ProfileConfig.getProfileDetail(name)`: the old body of `getActiveProfileDetail()` (copy the profile, strip the trailing `/` from REST endpoints), now for any name. `getActiveProfileDetail()` calls it.
- `stdio` and `ssh`: closing a session resets the module singleton only if it *is* the singleton, so closing a console no longer drops the shared session.
- `rest`: sessions from `createSession` do not save, reconnect to or clear `SAS.sessionId`, so a console never attaches to another console's (or the shared session's) compute session, and never clears its id.
- `PositronLanguageRuntimeSession.start()` uses `createSessionForProfile(this._profileName)`. Restart creates a fresh session, since `start()` runs again.
- Active session: SAS editors (`.xpt`/`.sas7bdat`) and the Assistant tools already go through the active `SASLanguageRuntimeSession` (its `SasClient` runs on that console's own session). Now the active session follows the foreground console (`onDidChangeForegroundSession`). Stopping a console clears the active session only if it is that console.
- `SupervisorAdapter` (not used, `USE_SUPERVISOR_APPROACH = false`) also uses `createSessionForProfile` and no longer changes the active profile setting.

## Remaining limits

- REST: the compute API configuration (`getApiConfig()`: base path, access token) is still global. Consoles against the same Viya server work. Consoles against *different* Viya servers at the same time are not supported (the SAS auth provider holds one account anyway).
- The status bar item is global: each session still updates it on connect and close.
- In Positron, the upstream code paths that still use `getSession()` (Library/Content navigators, notebooks, runs that cannot go to the console) use the shared session of the active profile, which is now separate from the consoles. With stdio, that means one more SAS process when those features are used.
- COM/IOM: each session has its own process, but they still share the stored password key, and closing one clears it.

## Testing

- New `client/test/positron-host/runtimeSessions.test.ts` (VS Code host, stdio with a fake SAS process through `processLauncher.spawn`):
  - "SAS (X)" spawns profile X's `saspath` while Y is active
  - two consoles of the same profile get two SAS processes
  - shutting down one console leaves the other's process running and able to run code, and it stays the active session

  These three tests fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- `client/test/connection/stdio` and `ssh`: `createSession` returns distinct sessions, separate from the shared one, and closing one keeps the shared one.
- Local: `npm run lint`, `npm run compile`, `npx tsc -p ./client` (no errors), `npm run test-positron` (198 passing), full `npm run test-client` (461 passing, 1 pending), `prettier --check` on changed files that were already formatted, `npm run copyright:check`.

Fixes #88, fixes #89

title: Positron: detect SAS 9.4 installs for the local stdio profile
description:
## Summary

In Positron, the `local` stdio profile was only added when SAS was installed at the SAS Analytics Pro path (`/opt/sas/viya/home/SASFoundation/sas`), so SAS 9.4 installs were missed. Detection now checks, in order, and uses the first executable candidate:

1. Paths in the new `SAS.localSasPaths` setting (string array, machine scope; relative paths ignored)
2. `/opt/sas/viya/home/SASFoundation/sas` (SAS Analytics Pro)
3. Common SAS 9.4 Foundation launchers: `/opt/sas/SASHome/SASFoundation/9.4/bin/sas_u8`, `/usr/local/SASHome/SASFoundation/9.4/bin/sas_u8`, `/opt/sasinside/SASHome/SASFoundation/9.4/bin/sas_u8`, `/opt/SASHome/SASFoundation/9.4/bin/sas_u8`
4. `sas` on `PATH` (looked up in Node by joining each absolute `PATH` entry, no shell)

The existing rules are unchanged: added once (globalState key), skipped if any stdio profile exists, made active only if no profile is active. `localSasProfile.ts` still has only type imports from `components/profile`. The executable check now also requires a regular file, so a `sas` directory on `PATH` does not match.

For SAS 9.4 the UTF-8 launcher `bin/sas_u8` is used rather than the `sas` script in `SASFoundation/9.4`, because the extension reads SAS output as UTF-8.

Docs: CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry; `sas9stdio.md` lists the detected paths and the setting, and explains why `sas_u8`.

`client/src/node/extension.ts` changes only the `localSasCandidates` import and call. The file is not Prettier-clean on `main`; it is left unformatted to avoid merge conflicts with upstream, so `prettier --check` is not run on it.

## Testing

- `npm run test-positron`: 207 passing (adds tests for the `sas_u8` paths, first-wins order, SAS 9.4 path, PATH fallback, extra paths from the setting, none found, candidate ordering and relative-path filtering)
- `npm run lint`, `npm run compile`, `tsc -p ./client`, `npx prettier --check` on changed files (except `extension.ts`), `npm run copyright:check`: pass
- `npm run test-client` is left to CI (it does not start on macOS)

title: Use the CHANGELOG.md section as the GitHub release notes
description:
## Summary

So that every release has the same notes as the changelog, without hand edits (0.3.1 and 0.4.0 needed them):

- **Package and Publish (`package.yml`):** creates the release with `--notes-file` built from the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section, not `--generate-notes`. If the release already exists, the workflow uploads the `.vsix` and resets the notes to the section. Notes are extracted before the tag is pushed, so a missing section fails without leaving a stray tag.
- **Pull Request Check (`pr.yml`):** when `package.json` has a version with no tag yet (a release PR), the check fails if `CHANGELOG.md` has no section for that version. Ordinary PRs, which carry the released version, skip it.
- **`tools/changelog-section.mjs <version>`:** prints the section between `## <version> - <date>` and the next `## ` heading, without leading and trailing blank lines. It exits 1 if the section is missing or empty.

## Testing

- `node tools/changelog-section.mjs 0.4.0` matches the notes now on the v0.4.0 release, and it also handles 0.3.1. A missing version (`9.9.9`) or no argument exits 1 with a message.
- The PR check step, simulated locally: with 0.4.0 it reports "already released"; with a new version that has no section it exits 1.
- Both workflow files are valid YAML and pass prettier. The release path itself only runs on the next version bump.

title: Add a stdio connection for local SAS (from upstream #1771)
description:
## Summary

Adds a `stdio` connection type for SAS installed on the same machine: the extension starts SAS directly (`sas -nodms -noterminal -nosyntaxcheck` over stdin/stdout), without SSH or SAS servers. This lets Positron use the SAS install in a SAS Analytics Pro image, for example in a Posit Workbench session started from one. Workbench licenses SAS for the session through `SASV9_OPTIONS`, which the stdio session inherits.

- **Upstream commit, unchanged:** sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension#1771 by Andreas Menrath, cherry-picked with authorship and DCO sign-off. SAS closed it for maintenance-scope reasons, not technical ones.
- **Fork wiring** (code paths upstream doesn't have):
  - Positron runtime managers: stdio sessions are located on the machine, like SSH.
  - View settings: no sign-in, library or server views for stdio, as for SSH.
  - `remoteTarget` returns `localhost` for stdio.
  - Posit Assistant's saspy export maps a stdio profile to saspy's STDIO access method.
- **Auto-detection (Positron):** when `/opt/sas/viya/home/SASFoundation/sas` exists, a `local` stdio profile is added once, so SAS shows up in the interpreter list without setup. It becomes active only if no profile is set. A deleted profile isn't added again, and an existing stdio profile is left alone.

Libraries in the Connections pane and the Data Explorer use `SasClient`, which runs plain SAS code through the session, so stdio sessions get them too.

## Testing

- Against real SAS in `sas/apro:2026.10` as a non-root user with `SASV9_OPTIONS` set, the PR's spawn and I/O logic worked: the `N?` prompt and the log arrive on stdout, the WORK marker on stderr, the run-end marker is seen, and the ODS HTML5 file is written to WORK.

title: Let Posit Assistant see SAS plots, tables and the Viewer
description:
Fixes #74. Stacked on #79, so this PR's diff shows only the #74 commits. It will be retargeted to `main` once #79 is merged.

## Cause
Research into posit.assistant 1.9.1 and the Positron 2026.10 workbench found three gaps:
- **Plots:** Posit Assistant sees a plot only through `positron.ai.getCurrentPlotUri()`. That returns only plots opened as a `positron.plot` comm with a pre-rendered image. A plain image output or HTML in the Viewer is invisible to it.
- **Text:** for code it runs itself, the Assistant reads only the stream text and the `text/plain` of the result. Ours was a fixed "SAS output produced (displayed in Viewer pane)".
- **Viewer:** the Assistant can read the Viewer with `positronViewer.read` and `positronViewer.screenshot` (Positron 2026.10 and later), but only for URL or HTML-file previews. Our report was a `createPreviewPanel` webview set to an HTML string, which Positron classes as content "agents can't read yet". The Assistant also only learns those commands from the `positron-commands` skill, which "what's in the Viewer?" doesn't trigger.

## Fix
- **PNG graphs:** console runs add `ods graphics / outputfmt=png;` to the ODS open line. This adds no new line, and the console log filter hides it. Graphs come back as inline PNGs instead of SVG.
- **Plots pane:** each PNG is opened as a `positron.plot` comm with `pre_render`. The `render`, `get_intrinsic_size` and `get_metadata` RPCs are answered with the same image, since SAS can't redraw at a new size. Plot comms are listed in `listClients` and closed by `removeClient` and on shutdown.
- **Viewer as a file:** the report is written to a temporary folder for each session and opened with `positron.window.previewHtml()`, which serves it through positron-proxy like R and Python HTML output.
  - The newest 20 files are kept (`outputFiles.ts`), and the folder is removed on shutdown.
  - If the file can't be shown, the report falls back to the webview.
- **Pane order:** the report opens first, and the run waits until it is visible (at most 3 seconds) before sending the plots. A run with graphs then ends with the Plots pane in front, as in R and Python. All of this happens before idle, which is when the Assistant looks for a new plot.
- **Text for the Assistant:** the result's `text/plain` holds a plain-text copy of the report: titles, tables as tab-separated rows, and `<pre>` listings, capped at 20,000 characters (`sasOutput.ts`). It also carries a short `text/html` note, which is what the console shows.
- **`sas-results` skill:** registered with `positron.ai.registerAgentSkillRoot` when that API exists (2026.10 and later). It tells the Assistant:
  - the log is in the Console, reports are in the Viewer (read them with `positronViewer.read`), and graphs are in the Plots pane (use `getPlot`);
  - to report a `not-found` command as "this Positron build is too old".
- The local `RuntimeClientType` values now match `positron.d.ts` (`positron.plot` and so on).

## Version notes
- On Positron 2026.09, plots and the text copy of code the Assistant runs reach it. Reading the Viewer, and so tables from code the user runs, needs 2026.10.
- Graphs in the Viewer report are now PNG rather than SVG.

## Testing
- New unit tests:
  - `sasOutput.test.ts`: PNG extraction, PNG size, HTML to text
  - `outputFiles.test.ts`: writing files, keeping the newest, cleanup
- `test-positron`: 192 passing. Lint, prettier and `tsc` are clean for the touched files.
- Checked live in Positron 2026.10 against Viya:
  - Plots show in the Plots pane, and the Assistant reads them with `getPlot`.
  - A plain "what's in the Viewer?" makes the Assistant read the report.
  - `plot.sas` and `test.sas` both end on the Plots pane.

title: Run SAS editor code in the Positron console
description:
Fixes #77.

## Cause
In Positron, Run, Run Selection and Run Region (F8, F3, toolbar, context menu) still used upstream's `runCode()`. Its `showResult()` opens a "Result" webview beside the editor, which split the editor area. Console runs already showed results in the Viewer.

## Fix
In Positron, `_run` (`client/src/commands/run.ts`) now hands SAS editor code to `positron.runtime.executeCode("sas", …)`, as Positron does for R and Python.
- The change to the upstream file is 4 lines. The logic is in the new `client/src/positron/runInConsole.ts`.
- **What runs:** the non-empty selections joined by newlines, the same rule as upstream's `getSelectedCode`. With no selection, the whole document runs.
- **Results:** they open in the Viewer, and the log goes to the console and the SAS Log channel.
- **Problems pane:** squiggles (#68) still map back to the file, because `buildSubmission()` finds the code in the active editor.
- **Upstream path kept for:**
  - Python, R and SQL files from SAS Content, which need SASCodeDocument's `proc python`, `proc r` and `proc sql` wrapping
  - runs without an active profile, so upstream still asks for one
- **Known difference:** the console path doesn't pass the file's folder as `baseDirectory`, which upstream does for ITC and SSH connections.

Also adds `executeCode` to the local `RuntimeManager` typings.

## Testing
- `consoleDiagnostics.test.ts`: `editorCodeToRun` with the whole document, one selection, several selections, and empty selections.
- `test-positron` passes. Lint, prettier and `tsc` are clean for the touched files. The node and browser builds pass.
- Checked live in Positron 2026.10 against Viya: F8 and F3 on a `.sas` file run in the console, the report opens in the Viewer, and no Result tab splits the editor.

title: Show the full SAS log for console runs
description:
Running `%put NOTE: user=&sysuserid;` in the SAS console printed only "✓ Done". Nothing appeared in the console or in any log.

## Cause
`emitLogMessage()` kept the console terse on purpose. It showed only errors, warnings and plain text, and dropped every line classified as a note or source echo. The full log was collected for diagnostics but never shown, and console runs never wrote to the SAS Log output channel.

## Fix
- **Console:** every log line of the user's code is streamed: source echo, NOTEs, `%put` output, warnings, errors. Streams are unchanged: errors and warnings go to stderr, everything else to stdout. Error and warning counting, the Fix/Explain error message and the audit status work as before.
- **Wrapper filter:** the new `client/src/positron/consoleLog.ts` hides the lines produced by Positron's wrapper:
  - `options source notes;`, the ODS open and close lines, `/** LOG_START_INDICATOR **/` and `%let _SASPROGRAMFILE`
  - source lines that hold only the traceability tag, the "Writing HTML5(VSCODE) Body file" note and the ITC markers

  When the user's code already contains its own `ods html5`, the tag sits on the user's first line, so it is stripped and the line is kept. The wrapper strings now live in this file, so `buildSubmission()` and the filter can't drift apart.
- **SAS Log channel:** the same lines are appended to "SAS Log: Console" through `appendSessionLogFn`. It doesn't auto-show the channel, so the panel stays on the Console. The run store isn't touched, so the editor Run command's clear-and-show behaviour is unchanged. Console logs build up across runs.
- The "✓ Done" summary is gone, since the log itself shows the run finished.

title: Deploy the docs from the pushed commit, not the version tag
description:
`deploy-doc.yml` runs on every push to `main` but builds the tag for the current `package.json` version. That has two problems:

- **Docs fixes only reach the site at the next release, and every merge in between republishes the tag.** After #75 merged, the deploy built `v0.3.0`, which has the old `baseUrl`, and republished the broken site. It took a manual push to `gh-pages` to fix it, and the next merge to `main` would have undone that.
- **It races `package.yml`.** On a release push, `package.yml` creates the `v<version>` tag while this workflow tries to check it out. On 2026-10-26 the deploy started before `v0.3.0` existed and failed at checkout.

This drops the `package-json-versioned-action` step and the `ref:`, so the checkout uses the pushed commit (or the ref chosen for a manual run).

The trade-off: the site now follows `main`, so docs for unreleased features are published as soon as they merge.

title: Release 0.3.0
description:
Release 0.3.0. Merging this PR tags `v0.3.0` and publishes the VSIX via `package.yml`.

Still based on SAS Extension for VS Code 1.21.0 (tag v1.21.0).

### Features

- SAS Clinical Acceleration Repository view: it is detected automatically when the active profile is a SAS Viya profile whose server runs the Clinical Repository service, and it uses the existing SAS Viya sign-in. You can browse, open (read-only), create folders, rename, upload or upload and expand, download, copy paths, and check out / undo check out. Actions that change an item (check out, rename, new folder, upload) are offered only where you have write permission, so read-only files still show Copy Path and Download. Ported from SAS's Clinical Acceleration extension for VS Code [#60](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-sas-extension/issues/60)
- Traceability of SAS console code, including code run by Positron Assistant [#58](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-sas-extension/issues/58):
  - New setting `SAS.audit.logFile`: when set, every console submission (user, host, Positron and Posit Workbench session, profile, code) and its outcome are appended to that file as JSON Lines
  - Each submission carries a `/* positron: user=… session=… exec=… */` comment, so it can be traced in the SAS log
  - The macro variables `&POSIT_USER`, `&POSIT_SESSION` and `&POSIT_WORKBENCH_SESSION` are set at session start
  - SAS Viya compute sessions are named `Positron SAS (<user>)` and carry the user and session ids as attributes. Each console job is named `positron-console`, and its description holds the user, session and execution ids

### Bug Fixes

- Errors and warnings from the SAS log now show as squiggles in the editor and in the Problems pane when you run code from a `.sas` file into the Positron console (Run Selection or the statement at the cursor). Code typed into the console or generated by Positron Assistant shows them in the console only [#68](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-sas-extension/issues/68)
- Data Explorer: SAS transport files (`.xpt`, XPORT v5 and v8/9, and PROC CPORT files) now open in the Data Explorer instead of as text. A file that holds several datasets asks which ones to open [#64](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-sas-extension/issues/64)
- Opening a `.sas7bdat` file now reports a failed LIBNAME (for example, a path the SAS server can't see) instead of an empty Data Explorer
- `.sas7bdat` and `.xpt` files opened from the Clinical Repository or SAS Content views now load in the Data Explorer: they are copied into the session's WORK directory first, which also works when SAS runs in lockdown

All changes were verified live on Posit Workbench with SAS Viya (lockdown) and SAS Clinical Acceleration.

title: Map SAS log problems from console runs back to the editor
description:
Fixes #68 (reproduced on Workbench: errors showed in the console, but not in the editor or the Problems pane).

## Cause
`execute()` built a `SASCodeDocument` from the whole active editor, but submitted Positron's own wrapper. `parseLog` anchors on the document's first wrapped line, `/** LOG_START_INDICATOR **/`, which was never sent, so it found no problems.

## Fix
`buildSubmission()` locates the console code in the active SAS editor (`locateCodeInDocument`).
- **If found** (Run Selection, or the statement at the cursor), the code is submitted as `codeDoc.getWrappedCode()` for a `SASCodeDocument` covering exactly that range:
  - Positron's ODS open lines and the traceability tag go in as `preamble`, and the closing line as `postamble`. `outputHtml: false`, so ODS isn't opened twice.
  - The log marker, the line offsets and the selection mapping then match what SAS echoes, and the existing upstream mapper does the rest.
  - As in VS Code, the submission now also sets `&_SASPROGRAMFILE`.
  - If the same code occurs more than once, the occurrence around (or just before) the cursor is used.
- **Otherwise** (typed in the console, Positron Assistant code), the previous wrapping is kept and no editor diagnostics are produced.

No upstream files change.

## Testing
- `client/test/positron/consoleDiagnostics.test.ts` covers the locator: single occurrence, trailing whitespace, repeated code chosen by cursor, not found.
- `client/test/positron-host/consoleDiagnostics.test.ts` is an end-to-end test. It builds the submission as `execute()` does, fakes the SAS log with a syntax-error indicator, and runs upstream's `parseLog` + `getLocationInRawCode`. The error maps to editor line 5 at the right column.
  - Run locally with a `Uri` shim (2 passing); it runs for real in CI's VS Code host.
- `test-positron`: 174 passing. Lint passes.
- **Live check still needed:** this changes what gets submitted for every run from an editor (the extra marker and `%let _SASPROGRAMFILE` lines).

title: Open datasets from the Clinical Repository and other non-local views
description:
Follow-up to #67 / #65, found while testing the Clinical Repository view:

- `.sas7bdat` failed with `ERROR: The path /PositLabs/Curanex-XR/data/adam is not in the list of accessible paths when SAS is in the lockdown state.`
- `.xpt` failed with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/PositLabs/Curanex-XR/data/adam/adae.xpt'`

## Cause
Both custom editors used `document.uri.fsPath`. For a `sasClinical:` URI that's the repository path. The sas7bdat viewer passed it to a LIBNAME on the compute server, and the xpt viewer tried to read it from local disk.

## Fix
For any **non-`file:`** URI (Clinical Repository, SAS Content, …), both editors now:
1. read the bytes through `workspace.fs.readFile(uri)`, so any file system provider works;
2. create a subdirectory under the session's WORK directory and read the WORK path back from the log (`buildWorkSubdirCode` / `parseWorkPath`);
3. **copy the file through SAS itself.** The bytes are sent as base64 `DATALINES` in about 1 MB chunks, decoded with `$BASE64X` and written with `RECFM=N` (`buildBase64WriteCode`). Later chunks append with `MOD`;
4. open it from there: `libname _FVWn '<work>/_fvwn'` for sas7bdat (lowercase file name, as SAS on UNIX requires), or the existing transport load code for xpt.

The first version used the compute Files API. On the test cluster it rejects WORK paths (`The path requested "…/SAS_work…/_fxptsrc/_fxpt1.xpt" is not available`) because it only serves the configured navigation roots. Going through SAS needs nothing beyond SAS being able to write WORK, which it always can, even in lockdown. It also works on every connection type, not just SAS Viya. Local files behave as before.

## Testing
- New unit tests:
  - WORK-path helpers and the libref pool prefix
  - the base64 transfer: lines decode back to the original bytes, including NULs, high bytes and trailing blanks; the DATA step's length arithmetic; chunk boundaries; create vs. append

  `test-positron`: 162 passing. `vsce package` (incl. lint) passes.
- **Not yet verified live.** Test VSIX built locally from this branch.

title: Offer Clinical Repository write actions only where the user may write
description:
Follow-up to #67. While testing, check-out failed on the server with *"File was not checked out because you do not have write permission on the file."* That happens because the view offered every action on every item. Every file stays visible; only actions that need write access now depend on the user's permissions.

## How
- **Effective permissions per item:** `GET /clinicalRepository/authorizations/{id}/permissions`, the endpoint SAS's own Clinical Acceleration extension uses (`RepositoryModel.getPermission`). It isn't in the public v3 spec, but it is listed in the service's live root links.
- **Alternatives considered and rejected:**
  - Reading rights from item links: the spec has no `update` / `delete` rels on items.
  - Inheriting a folder's rights: CA has per-item ACLs, so that would be wrong for files with their own permissions.
  - Evaluating `/repository/items/{id}/permissions`: that returns the item's ACL, not the user's effective rights, and would need group membership resolved on the client.
- **Lookups are asynchronous:**
  - The tree renders immediately, with write actions hidden (`;permUnknown;`).
  - Lookups are cached per item, run at most 8 at a time, and re-render only that item when they return (`;canWrite;` / `;readOnly;`).
  - VS Code has no hook before a context menu opens, so the lookup can't be deferred to the right-click.
- **Fail-open:** if the endpoint can't be used (404, 5xx, network error, unrecognised response), all actions are shown as before, the server keeps enforcing its rules, and this is logged once to "SAS Clinical Repository". A 403 on the lookup counts as read-only. Refresh clears the cache.

## Menu rules
| Action | Requires |
|---|---|
| New Folder, Upload, Upload and Expand | container + `canWrite` |
| Check out ▸ | `canWrite` + (container or not checked out) |
| Rename | `canWrite` + `canRename` |
| Undo Check out | unchanged: your own check-outs, plus containers |
| Copy Path, Download | always |

## Testing
- `parseWritePermission` (array / delimited string / object shapes; unrecognised responses)
- the concurrency limiter (peak never exceeds the limit; a failure frees its slot)
- context tokens
- the package.json menu evaluation for read-only, unknown and writable items
- `RepositoryModel` (CI host tests): lookup URL, per-item caching, 403 → read-only, fail-open with a single log line and no further lookups, the concurrency cap, and a retry after a non-permission failure

`test-positron`: 170 passing. Lint and `vsce package` pass. Not yet verified live; test VSIX built locally.

title: Add the SAS Clinical Acceleration Repository view
description:
Fixes #60.

## What it does
When the active SAS profile is a **SAS Viya (REST) profile whose server runs SAS Clinical Acceleration**, a **Clinical Repository** view appears in the SAS sidebar, below SAS Content and SAS Server. There is nothing to configure. It reuses the existing SAS Viya sign-in; there's no separate CA profile or login.

Context menu, matching the issue screenshot:

| Group | Actions |
|---|---|
| New | New Folder… |
| Check out | Check out to Workspace ▸ (With Content / Without Content), Undo Check out |
| Copy | Copy Path |
| Modify | Rename… |
| Transfer | Download…, Upload…, Upload and Expand… |

The view title has Refresh and Collapse All. Clicking a file opens it read-only through a `sasClinical:` file system. Checked-out files get a **CO** badge, with a tooltip for "you" or "<user>". Copy to Workspace, Delete, and the Workspace / Properties / Version History views are left out of this first version.

## Detection
`GET {endpoint}/clinicalRepository/`. The trailing slash matters: without it the server answers 302. The probe uses `maxRedirects: 0` and a 5 s timeout, and sends the token only if a SAS session already exists; it never prompts.

| Response | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 + JSON | available |
| 401/403 without a token | service is there; the view waits for `SAS.authorized` |
| 403 with a token | user has no CA access; hidden |
| 404 / 3xx | no CA; hidden |
| 5xx / network error | hidden, retried after 30 s, 1, 2 and 5 min |

The probe re-runs on `SAS.connectionProfiles` changes, on SAS sign-in changes, and on Refresh. It is debounced, and stale results are dropped.

The context key is `SAS.clinicalAvailable`. IDs (`SAS.clinical.*`, `clinicalrepositorydataprovider`, `sasClinical:`) don't clash with SAS's own CA extension, so both can be installed at once.

## Implementation
Ported from [sassoftware/vscode-sas-ca-extension](https://github.com/sassoftware/vscode-sas-ca-extension) (Apache-2.0, SAS headers kept plus an "Adapted from" note) into the fork-only `client/src/clinical/`. The API facts the viyar work verified live (sol-eng/viyar#7) are built in: root via `repository/paths?path=/`, paging via `next` links (`count` is the page size, not the total), and content via `POST …/content`, which may come back zipped. Bugs fixed while porting:
- Children paging re-requested the first page instead of following `next`.
- File content was decoded as text, which corrupted binaries. Zipped single files are unpacked.
- New Folder sent its headers object as the request body.
- `closeFileIfOpen` used `find(async …)` and so always matched the first tab.
- Upload-and-expand checked an array with `!success`, so failures went unreported.

Shared upstream files: one registration line in `client/src/node/extension.ts`, plus append-only `package.json` / `package.nls.json` contributions.

## Testing
- `client/test/positron/clinicalUtils.test.ts` covers:
  - paging across pages, plus the loop and page-limit guards
  - the probe classification table
  - context values, **checked against the actual `when` clauses in package.json**
  - zip extraction (deflated, stored, directory entries)
  - validators
- `client/test/positron/clinicalActionStatus.test.ts` covers polling: done, ERROR, timeout, cancel, HTTP errors.
- `client/test/clinical/RepositoryModel.test.ts` (VS Code host, axios stubbed) covers root and children, the folder body, rename `If-Match`, upload query, single and bulk download, checkout and undo batch bodies plus polling, and non-Viya profiles.
- `test-positron`: 128 passing. Compile, server bundle smoke test, lint and copyright check all pass. `test-client` couldn't run locally (macOS killed the downloaded VS Code), so it relies on CI here.
- **Not yet verified live.** `https://caf.pcluster.soleng.posit.it/clinicalRepository/` currently returns **503** (routed, but the service isn't serving), while `/SASClinicalRepository/` and `/compute/` return 401. Once the service is back, please check:
  - [ ] View appears after sign-in; hidden for an SSH profile
  - [ ] Open a .sas file and a binary file (raw vs. zipped single-file content)
  - [ ] New Folder / Rename (`PATCH` content type and `If-Match` accepted?) / Upload / Upload and Expand / Download
  - [ ] Check out with and without content, Undo check out; CO badge
  - [ ] Multi-select download (`/repository/files/content` is inferred from the docs)

title: Make SAS console submissions traceable to user and session
description:
Fixes #58.

Every console submission is traced, whether typed, run from an editor, or generated by Positron Assistant. All of these go through `SASLanguageRuntimeSession.execute()`. Silent internal queries (Data Explorer, Connections pane) are not traced, because the extension generates them itself.

## Local audit log
New setting **`SAS.audit.logFile`**: machine scope, empty by default, so it is off unless set. `~` expands to the home directory. When set, two JSON Lines records are written per submission:
```json
{"event":"input","ts":"…","osUser":"jdoe","host":"wb-node-1","positronSessionId":"…","profile":"Viya","connectionType":"rest","workbenchServerUrl":"…","workbenchSessionId":"…","sasUser":"jdoe","executionId":"…","code":"proc print …"}
{"event":"complete","ts":"…","positronSessionId":"…","executionId":"…","status":"ok","errorCount":0,"warningCount":1,"durationMs":812}
```
Writes are serialised. A failing write warns once and never blocks execution.

## SAS-side tags
- **All backends:**
  - A `/* positron: user=… session=… exec=… */` comment goes on the **first line** of each submission, so it lands in the SAS log without adding a line.
  - `&POSIT_USER`, `&POSIT_SESSION` and `&POSIT_WORKBENCH_SESSION` are set at session start.
- **SAS Viya:**
  - Compute sessions are created with the name `Positron SAS (<user>)`, a description, and the attributes `client`, `osUser`, `host`, `positronSessionId` and `workbench*`. This also replaces the `mysess` placeholder on the `serverId` path.
  - Console jobs get the name `positron-console` and a description with the user, session and execution id.
  - On ITC, the second `run()` argument is a `skipPageHeaders` flag, so job tags are passed only for REST.

Shared upstream files change only by adding optional `sessionTags` (on `BaseConfig`) and `jobTags` (on the REST run args).

## Please check
- [x] **Workbench session id variable:** confirmed in a Workbench 2026.09 Positron Pro session. Workbench is detected via `RS_SERVER_URL`. The id comes from `RS_SESSION_URL` (`/s/<id>/`), falling back to `RSTUDIO_SESSION_SCOPE_PROJECT` + `RSTUDIO_SESSION_SCOPE_ID`.
- [ ] **SSH:** the tagged first line can exceed 80 characters. The <80 rule in `execute()` protects the ODS `body=` line, and user code lines are often longer, so this should be fine. Still worth a quick SSH run.
- [ ] **Viya:** `GET /compute/sessions/{id}` shows the name and attributes; `GET /compute/sessions/{id}/jobs` shows the job name and description.

Unrelated issue found along the way: Positron console diagnostics anchor on `/** LOG_START_INDICATOR **/` (`SASCodeDocument`). The Positron execute path never sends that marker, so log-based squiggles from console runs probably never show. This PR doesn't touch it.

## Testing
New `sessionIdentity.test.ts` and `auditLog.test.ts`. `test-positron`: 115 passing. `npm run compile` succeeds. Not yet run against a live session.

title: Open SAS transport (.xpt) files in the Data Explorer
description:
Fixes #64.

## What changed
- New custom editor `sas.xptViewer` for `*.xpt`. It reads the 80-byte header to tell the formats apart:
  - **XPORT v5** (`LIBRARY HEADER RECORD`), loaded via `libname … xport` + `proc copy`
  - **XPORT v8/9** (`LIBV8 HEADER RECORD`), loaded via `%xpt2loc`
  - **PROC CPORT** (`**COMPRESSED**`), loaded via `proc cimport`
  - Anything else shows a "not a SAS transport file" message.
- Each file is unpacked into its own library in a WORK subdirectory (`_FXPT1`, `_FXPT2`, …), so two open files never clobber each other. XPORT is a sequential engine and the Data Explorer re-reads pages, counts and dictionary metadata, which is why the data is copied once.
- A file holding several datasets shows a multi-select QuickPick. Tabs are titled `adae.xpt: ADAE`.
- SAS `ERROR:` lines from the load are shown in the editor tab. The `.sas7bdat` viewer now does the same instead of opening an empty Data Explorer.
- `xpt`/`cpt` are treated as binary in Data Connections, and `xpt` gets the dataset icon in SAS Server Files.

Same limitation as `.sas7bdat`: the client-side path is sent to SAS as-is, so the SAS server has to see the same filesystem.

## Testing
- New unit tests `client/test/positron/xptFormat.test.ts` (header detection, generated SAS code, quoting, libref allocation, log error parsing). `test-positron`: 113 passing.
- Not yet verified against a live SAS session. Quick check: `libname x xport '/tmp/class.xpt'; proc copy in=sashelp out=x; select class heart; run;`, then open `/tmp/class.xpt` from the Explorer.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump webpack from 5.107.2 to 5.108.3
description:
Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 5.107.2 to 5.108.3.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v5.108.3

Patch Changes

  • Speed up CSS parsing and reduce CSS AST node memory. (by @​alexander-akait in #21285)

  • Fix HMR codegen crash for harmony accept with unresolved imports. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #21302)

  • Match harmony accept dependencies by module reference so HMR codegen handles imports without a module or chunk id. (by @​alexander-akait in #21303)

v5.108.2

Patch Changes

  • Fix lazy barrel deferral of ungrouped side-effect imports. (by @​hai-x in #21291)

  • Respect the node: prefix for node.js core modules used as externals. (by @​alexander-akait in #21286)

v5.108.1

Patch Changes

  • Fix invalid property access for escaped namespace imports with multi-character mangled export names. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #21280)

  • Add frames to ProfilingPlugin TracingStartedInBrowser event so the trace loads in Chrome DevTools. (by @​alexander-akait in #21269)

v5.108.0

Minor Changes

  • Treat top-level await and import.meta as ES module markers, matching Node.js syntax detection so no explicit module type is needed. (by @​alexander-akait in #21218)

  • Add a bun target that emits ESM and externalizes bun:* and node.js built-in modules. (by @​alexander-akait in #21248)

  • Support CommonJS reexports via Object.defineProperty value and getter descriptors. (by @​alexander-akait in #21129)

  • Support JSON Schema const when generating CLI flags from a schema. (by @​alexander-akait in #21087)

  • Support JSON Schema if/then/else when generating CLI flags from a schema. (by @​alexander-akait in #21087)

  • Skip import specifiers, require() and import() calls in dead conditional branches gated by inlined imported constants (isDEV ? A : B), evaluated via getCondition. (by @​hai-x in #21136)

  • CSS localIdentName [hash] now resolves to the local ident hash (matching css-loader); use [modulehash] for the module hash. (by @​alexander-akait in #21259)

  • Add CSS parser as option and resolve url() inside HTML style attributes. (by @​alexander-akait in #21157)

  • Add dedicated module classes for all built-in module types. (by @​alexander-akait in #21164)

  • Support .html/.css for the default ./src entry under the html/css experiments. (by @​alexander-akait in #21039)

  • Add defineConfig helper for typed configuration files. (by @​alexander-akait in #21169)

  • Add a deno target (with versions, e.g. deno, deno2, deno1.40) that emits ESM, resolves node.js built-ins via the required node: specifier, and keeps Deno's own import protocols (npm:, jsr:, node:, http(s)://) external. (by @​alexander-akait in #21247)

title: Add Positron API integration tests and CI workflow
description:
## Summary
Closes https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14966

Adds a Positron-only integration test suite that runs the SAS extension inside a **real Positron build** via [`@posit-dev/positron-test-electron`](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-test-electron), plus a CI workflow that runs it on every PR and push to `main`.

Part of the rollout tracked in posit-dev/positron#14531 (pattern established in quarto-dev/quarto#1058 and posit-dev/publisher#4298).

## What's covered

The tests exercise the extension's real Positron integration (`client/src/positron/`) against the live API — paths unreachable by the plain VS Code suite (`test-client`) or the mocked-vscode unit tests (`test-positron`):

- **`extension.test.ts`** — Positron injects the `acquirePositronApi` global, the extension's own `isPositron()` / `getPositronApi()` helpers detect it, and the extension activates in the Positron extension host.
- **`runtime-discovery.test.ts`** — the heart of the integration: each `SAS.connectionProfiles` entry is surfaced to Positron as a language runtime by `SASLanguageRuntimeManager`, `getPreferredRuntime("sas")` resolves to one, and the configuration watcher re-discovers runtimes when profiles change. All metadata-level, so no SAS server or session is needed. Profile seeding is self-healing against the unawaited default write in `ProfileConfig.validateSettings()`.

## Harness

- `tools/run-positron-tests.mjs` downloads/caches a Positron build (stable by default; `POSITRON_CHANNEL` / `POSITRON_VERSION` supported) and runs the Mocha entry point (`client/test/positron-api/index.ts`) inside it.
- Run locally with `npm run test-positron-api` (`@posit-dev/positron-test-electron@0.0.3` ships macOS/Linux/Windows platform descriptors). On a headless Linux machine, wrap it: `xvfb-run -a npm run test-positron-api` — Positron is an Electron app and needs a display server.
- The suite is named `positron-api` because `test-positron` / `client/test/positron/` were already taken by the mocked-vscode unit tests; `client/test/index.ts` excludes it from the plain VS Code suite.
- `client/test/positron-api/README.md` documents how to run and add tests.

## CI

`.github/workflows/positron-api-tests.yml`: **ubuntu-latest** (Linux Actions minutes bill at ~1/10 the macOS rate — posit-dev/positron#15281; same pattern as posit-dev/shiny-vscode#116 and TidierOrg/positron-julia#43), `posit-dev/setup-positron@v1`, test command wrapped in `xvfb-run -a`, cache of the Positron download keyed by `runner.os` + channel + date (the cache layout is per-platform, so an OS-less key could restore another OS's build and suppress the save). Triggers on PRs and pushes to `main`, plus `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs once merged (the sibling `deploy-doc` workflow uses the same trigger).

**Verified on this PR's own check run** (ubuntu-latest, stable Positron 2026.08.1-2, 2m31s total): https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-sas-extension/actions/runs/32180303088

```
Run Positron API tests   xvfb-run -a npm run test-positron-api
Run Positron API tests     6 passing (4s)
Run Positron API tests   Exit code:   0
```

(The earlier macOS-runner version of the workflow was also proven green before the switch: run [30030583441](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron-sas-extension/actions/runs/30030583441).)

## Build fix required along the way

TypeScript 6's strict defaults had broken `tsc -p ./client` (the shared `pretest` step) with hundreds of pre-existing errors. Fixed minimally: `strict: false` + `skipLibCheck: true` in `client/tsconfig.json`, and a `*.css` ambient declaration for TS6's new side-effect-import check (TS2882). No emitted-code changes.

## Testing

- 6/6 tests pass in CI on ubuntu-latest against a downloaded stable Positron, log-verified `6 passing` + `Exit code: 0` (run linked above)
- 6/6 pass locally inside an installed Positron on Windows
- Vanilla `test-client` suite verified unaffected (same pre-existing local failures with and without this change; the new tests are correctly excluded)
- Lint, copyright check, and Prettier clean on all new/changed files

## Known issue / follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **The failing `build` check is pre-existing**: `npm run format:check` fails on ~285 files on `main` (the tree was formatted with a different Prettier version than the lockfile pins), so the Pull Request Check workflow is red for every PR — including all recent dependabot PRs — before tests even run. Needs a standalone repo-wide reformat (or a Prettier version pin) so it doesn't pollute feature diffs.
- **Migrate to the published `@posit-dev/positron` package**: it's already a devDependency (and marked external in both bundlers) but never imported — the extension hand-rolls its own API types (`client/src/positron/positron-types.ts`) and `tryAcquirePositronApi()` helper. The new tests deliberately go through those same hand-rolled helpers so they cover what actually runs today; when the migration happens, only their imports need updating. (Same follow-up shape as posit-dev/publisher#3647.)

title: Show column distributions for SAS tables in the Data Explorer (#55)
description:
## Summary
Fixes #55.

**Root cause:** Positron reads `get_column_profiles.supported_types` as `{profile_type, support_status}` objects; `isHistogramSupported()` does `.find(s => s.profile_type === "small_histogram")`. The SAS backend sent plain strings (`["null_count", "summary_stats"]`), so Positron never requested histograms or frequency tables. The backend didn't implement them either.

**Changes**
- `get_state`: advertises all six profile types in the object format.
- **Histograms** (`small_histogram` / `large_histogram`, numeric columns):
  - `getColumnBinningStats` gets n/min/max/Q1/Q3 via `PROC MEANS`, plus a non-integer count.
  - `computeHistogramBins` chooses bins the way Positron's Python backend does: Freedman–Diaconis capped at `num_bins`, Sturges when the IQR is 0, a single `[v, v]` bin for constant columns, and no more bins than distinct integers for integer columns.
  - `getColumnHistogramCounts` counts all requested histograms with `PROC SQL` in one submission. Small and large histograms share the stats.
- **Frequency tables** (`small_frequency_table` / `large_frequency_table`, character columns): `PROC FREQ`, top `limit` values plus `other_count`. Columns are aliased (`_fv<i>`) so a column named `COUNT` can't clash with `PROC FREQ` output. Values are truncated to 60 characters to stay under the SSH line-wrap width.
- **String summary stats** for character columns: `num_unique`, `num_empty`.
- **Row filter:** applied to every profile query. `PROC MEANS` / `PROC FREQ` read a `PROC SQL` view, so filters have the same semantics as before (e.g. `LIKE … ESCAPE`).
- **Bug fix:** `getColumnNullCounts` / `getColumnSummaryStats` built macro names like `_mean_<column>`, which exceeded SAS's 32-character limit for column names longer than about 26 characters. All profile queries now use indexed names.

**Not in scope:** date/datetime summary stats (`date_stats`). Positron requests no sparkline for dates, and their behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification
_Live checks verified by @michaelmayer2 on Positron 2026.10 with SAS Viya._

- [x] 21 new or updated unit tests: binning (FD, IQR = 0, constant, integer cap, `num_bins` cap, empty); record parsers, including values with `|` and noise lines; every query keeps macro names ≤ 32 characters with a 32-character column name; `get_state` shape; profile assembly; row filter passed to every query. 101 passing.
- [x] Lint clean, no new type errors (640 before and after), smoke test passes.
- [x] Live, Positron 2026.10 + Viya: SASHELP.CLASS sparklines and expanded views, row filter, 32-character column names, SASHELP.CARS responsiveness.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Hide the unused Libraries view in Positron (#54)
description:
## Summary
Fixes #54.

All five views in the SAS sidebar were guarded with `&& !positron.context`. **No such context key exists**: neither Positron nor the extension sets it, so the guard was always true. In Positron, `LibraryNavigator` is created without a tree (`new LibraryNavigator(context, !isPositron())`), because libraries are shown in the Connections / Data Connections pane. That left an empty **Libraries** view.

- `librarydataprovider`: guarded with Positron's built-in constant context key **`isPositron`**. Positron sets it to `true` (`CONSTANT_VALUES.set("isPositron", true)`); VS Code doesn't define it, so it's false there.
- The other four views: the no-op guard is removed. SAS Content and SAS Server *do* work in Positron, and SAS Content isn't available anywhere else, so they stay. Their `when` clauses now match upstream v1.21.0 exactly, which means less fork divergence to carry.

## Verification
_Live checks verified by @michaelmayer2 on Positron 2026.10 with SAS Viya._

- [x] Positron 2026.10: the SAS sidebar shows SAS Content / SAS Server / Sign In, with no Libraries view.
- [x] CI `test-client` (VS Code): views unaffected.

title: Merge upstream SAS Extension for VS Code v1.21.0
description:
## Summary
Merges upstream **SAS Extension for VS Code v1.21.0** (`7d14ab4`) into the fork. This is a merge, not a rebase, so `main`'s published history is untouched.

**Fork base:** upstream `main` at `2e74e19`, 28 commits after v1.19.1 and before v1.20.0. The CHANGELOG previously said "1.19.1 (e954c7f)", but `e954c7f` is a dependabot commit in this fork. The local tag `v1.19.1` in some clones points at a fork commit (`a3f73d8`); upstream's v1.19.1 is `b649b4b`.

This brings in 108 upstream commits (v1.20.0 and v1.21.0) across 106 files.

## Conflicts and how they were resolved
No source files conflicted. The overlapping files (`client/src/node/extension.ts`, `client/src/connection/session.ts`, the LibraryNavigator and ContentNavigator files, workflows) merged automatically. I reviewed upstream's changes to them; they don't touch the fork's Positron code.

| File(s) | Resolution |
|---|---|
| `package.json` (root) | Fork identity kept; higher version of each shared dependency. Also fixes the `"description "` key (trailing space), so the extension now has a description. |
| `client/package.json` | Upstream versions (incl. **ag-grid 35 → 36**); fork-only `@posit-dev/positron` kept |
| `server/package.json` | Fork's `vscode-languageserver ^10.0.0-next.18` (used by the #46 bundling alias); upstream's `vscode-languageserver-textdocument 1.0.14` |
| `website/package.json` + lock | Upstream |
| `l10n/bundle.l10n.*.json` (7) | Upstream wording; verified every hunk has the same keys on both sides |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Fork changelog, plus a new Unreleased entry for this update |
| Root, client and server lockfiles | Regenerated with `npm install` |

New upstream behaviour worth knowing: download menu items are now hidden unless `SAS.allowDownload` is set. `extension.ts` defaults it to `true` (checked after the merge), and Viya compute contexts can override it.

title: Data Connections pane: SAS libraries (#47, from #49) and SAS Server Files
description:
## Summary

Brings the Data Connections work onto `main` and adds SAS Server Files to the new pane.

**Why #49's commit is in here:** #49 was stacked on #48 and merged into `fix/issues-45-46` instead of `main`, because its base wasn't retargeted after #48 merged. Its commit `ed69050` is therefore not on `main` yet, and this PR carries it unchanged. Fixes #47.

### 1. SAS libraries in the Data Connections pane (`ed69050`, already reviewed in #49)
On Positron 2026.10+ with `dataConnections.enabled` on, a `SasDataConnectionsDriver` is registered via `positron.dataConnections.registerDriver`. On 2026.09 and earlier, or with the setting off, the legacy Connections pane comm is used, unchanged. See #49 for details.

### 2. SAS Server Files in the Data Connections pane (`9bcb3e2`, new)
- For REST (Viya) profiles, each session also reports a **SAS Server Files (profile)** connection. The legacy pane shows it as before.
- Folders use `directory` nodes and can be browsed. Files use `file` nodes. Positron only previews tables and views, so clicking a file opens the **details editor** instead: path, size, modified time, and the content as a code section highlighted by language. Content is shown only for text files up to 512 KB; binary files (`.sas7bdat`, `.xlsx`, `.pdf`, …) and larger files show properties only.
- The Compute file system calls move into a shared `ServerFilesBrowser` used by both the legacy comm and the new driver. Server path construction is unchanged, including `fileNavigationRoot: CUSTOM`.
- The mechanism gains a `content` option parameter (`libraries` / `files`, default `libraries`).

## Verification
- [x] 4 new unit tests (server files discovery, missing files, browse and details, binary/size limits). 80 passing (`TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`). Lint is clean.
- [x] Libraries in the Data Connections pane verified live on Positron 2026.10 with Viya (in #49).
- [x] Server Files in the Data Connections pane verified live on Positron 2026.10 with Viya: folders browse, and file details show the content.
- [ ] Legacy pane (2026.09, or `dataConnections.enabled: false`): not yet tried live. Server Files there now goes through `ServerFilesBrowser`.

title: CI: run the test suites; make format and client type-check non-blocking
description:
## Summary
CI never ran any tests on this fork. `npm run format:check` failed first. Behind it, `npm run test` also failed in `pretest` on the client type-check: 638 pre-existing strict-mode errors, mostly in files shared with upstream `sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension`.

Fixing either one would mean reformatting or editing shared files, which would cause conflicts on every upstream sync. So this PR changes only `.github/workflows/pr.yml`:

| Step | Mode |
|---|---|
| `format:check` | non-blocking, reported in the log |
| `copyright:check`, `compile` | blocking |
| `test-server`, `test-positron` (transpile-only*) | blocking |
| `test-server-bundle` (language server smoke test from #48) | blocking |
| `tsc -p ./client` | non-blocking, reported in the log; still emits `client/out` |
| `test-client` (VS Code integration tests) | blocking |
| `vsce package` | blocking |

\* The test tsconfigs lack mocha and node types (TS2593/TS2591), and Node 22+ needs `--no-experimental-strip-types` for ts-node. Both are set as step `env`, so `package.json` is untouched.

## Verification
CI run on this PR: 4 server tests, 80 Positron tests, the smoke test (17 semantic tokens), and **237 VS Code integration tests (1 pending, 0 failing)** all pass. The format and type-check steps fail as expected and are only reported.
