This adds a Data Connections driver and keeps the legacy path, so the extension works with both panes:

| Positron | `dataConnections.enabled` | Path used |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.10+ | on (default) | New `SasDataConnectionsDriver` via `positron.dataConnections.registerDriver` |
| 2026.10+ | off | Legacy `positron.connection` comm (unchanged) |
| 2026.09 and earlier | n/a (no API) | Legacy `positron.connection` comm (unchanged) |

The choice is made once at activation (`isDataConnectionsPaneActive`), matching Positron, which also reads the setting once at startup.

### New pane
- Each running SAS console session registers itself as a source (`addSource`) and is reported through `discoverConnections()`. `onDidChange` fires when sessions start or end. If a session restarts, the connection follows it.
- Libraries are shown as schemas, members as tables or views, and columns as fields (`char(n)` / `num`). Everything goes through the `SasClient` methods fixed in #48. Preview opens the existing Data Explorer.
- `client/src/positron/positron-types.ts` gets local typings for the subset of the API used. The bundled `@posit-dev/positron` 0.2.4 has no `dataConnections` namespace.

### Not covered yet
- The "SAS Server Files" connection for REST profiles still uses only the legacy comm, so it doesn't show up in the new pane.

## Verification
- [x] 9 new unit tests (`sasDataConnections.test.ts`): detection matrix, discovery and change events, session restart, missing session, library/member/column tree, preview, disconnect. 76 passing in total (`TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`).
- [x] Positron 2026.10.0 (build 297) with Viya: SAS (Viya) appears in Data Connections. SASHELP lists every member, which also confirms #45, and preview opens the Data Explorer.
- [ ] Legacy pane: not yet run live on 2026.09 or with `dataConnections.enabled: false`. That code path is unchanged.

Stacked on #48 (base `fix/issues-45-46`); retarget to `main` once #48 is merged.

title: Fix language server crash (#46), truncated Connections pane listings (#45) and Viya sign-in callback
description:
## Summary

Fixes #46 and #45, plus two Viya sign-in fixes found while verifying them.

### #46: no SAS syntax highlighting (language server crashed on startup)
SAS highlighting mostly comes from LSP semantic tokens. `a3f73d8` marked `vscode-languageserver/lib/common/progress` as external in both bundlers (esbuild and webpack). `pyright-internal` requires that file, but `node_modules` isn't shipped in the VSIX, so the v0.1.0 server crashed right away with `Cannot find module 'vscode-languageserver/lib/common/progress'`. That broke highlighting, completion, formatting and folding.

- `tools/build.mjs`, `webpack.config.js`: alias the deep import to its real file so it is bundled. It had been externalized because the package's `exports` map doesn't expose it.
- New `tools/smoke-server.mjs` (`npm run test-server-bundle`, added to `pr.yml`): starts the built server, opens a SAS document and requests semantic tokens.
- `configurationDefaults`: the default SAS formatter pointed to the upstream `SAS.sas-lsp`; it is now `posit.positron-sas`.

### #45: Connections pane only shows ~15 tables
The metadata queries in `sasClient.ts` put every name into one `|`-separated macro variable and printed it with a single `%put`. The SAS log wraps that at `LINESIZE` (~132 chars ≈ 15 SASHELP names), and the wrapped remainder was then parsed as the *types* line. Wide tables lost columns the same way, which also affected Data Explorer and the assistant tools.

- `getLibraryList`, `getLibraryMembers` and `getDatasetColumns` now emit one prefixed record per `%put` (`LIB=`, `MEM=name|type`, `COL=name|type|len|fmt`). This is the pattern `getDatasetRows` already uses, and it also avoids the 64K macro-variable limit.
- New tests: a 200-member library, a 100-column table, noise lines mixed in, and an empty library.

### Viya sign-in
- The OAuth callback was hardcoded to `<scheme>://sas.sas-lsp`, the upstream extension's ID, so a code sent back to Positron could never reach this extension. It is now built from the running extension's ID.
- The URI handler is now registered *before* the browser opens, so a fast redirect from an existing SSO session can't arrive before anything is listening.
- New "SAS Authentication" log channel: callback URL, authorize request and received URIs, with codes and PKCE values redacted.

## Verification
- [x] Smoke test passes against the server extracted from the packaged VSIX (17 semantic tokens). The v0.1.0 server fails it (exit code 1).
- [x] The browser bundle contains no external reference to the module.
- [x] `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true npm run test-positron`: 67 passing.
- [x] `vsce package` succeeds, including the lint in `vscode:prepublish`.
- [x] Viya sign-in tested on Positron 2026.10. It works with the built-in `vscode` client; a custom client must be registered with a matching redirect URI.
- [ ] **#45 is not verified in a live session.** On Positron 2026.10 the new Data Connections pane disposes runtime connection comms, so no SAS connection shows up at all (#47). Covered by unit tests only.
- [ ] **The automatic callback is not verified.** The Viya instance used for testing showed the code for pasting instead of redirecting to Positron. The callback-ID fix is correct, but its effect hasn't been observed.

## Known CI issues already on `main`
- `npm run format:check` already fails on 63 files on `main`. To keep this diff focused, only new files are formatted here.
- `npm run test-positron` fails type-checking on `main` because the mocha globals aren't in the tsconfig types (TS2593). It passes in transpile-only mode.

Fixes #45
Fixes #46
Related: #47

v10.0.0

💥 Breaking Changes

  • Dropped support for Node.js <22.0.0. Older Node.js version have reached end-of-life, and certain features require new-ish JS APIs.
  • concurrently is now ESM-only. It's now possible to require(esm). See here for interoperability.
  • Prefix colors now default to automatic - #581 The colors used to default to reset (which does nothing). Concurrently now automatically selects a color, out of the box. The list of colors used is not jarring nor carries semantic meaning, and reads well in both dark and light terminal backgrounds.
  • Removed deprecated flags and options
    • CLI flag --name-separator: use commas instead.
    • API option killOthers: use killOthersOn instead.

✨ New Features

  • Support applying modifiers to hex prefix colors (e.g. #ff0000.bold) - #450
  • Support chalk's color functions in prefixes (e.g. rgb(), hex(), bgRgb(), etc) - #578
  • Set prefix background color via bg#RRGGBB - #578
  • Allow shell override via --shell CLI flag/shell API option - #288, #589, #556 concurrently distinguishes between cmd.exe, powershell, and POSIX-based shells.
  • Manual prefix coloring in templates e.g. [{color}{name}{/color}] - #583, #587

🐛 Bug fixes

  • Scope quote normalization to CLI input - #582, #585 It should now also be possible to run commands like "/some/command" foo bar"
  • Don't throw when color doesn't exist - #580

🔐 Security

title: feat: Posit Assistant integration
description:
Register SAS metadata tools with Positron's language model API and
provide workspace context so the assistant understands the SAS session:
- sas_list_libraries: discover available libraries
- sas_list_tables: list datasets/views in a library
- sas_describe_table: column names, types, and row count
- sas_export_saspy_config: export profile as saspy config for Quarto
- Workspace context provider feeds session state to the assistant
- Session context updates automatically on start/stop

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

**Summary:**
Posit(ron) Assistant integration 

**Testing:**
1. Install Extension and make sure you have a valid connection to SAS via SASConnection in User settings.json
2. Start a SAS session
3. Run `PROC NONSENSE;` on the console to see an error with `Fix/Explain` Links 
4. Click on Fix or Explain to get Positron assistants analysis of your error 
5. Additionally do an exploratory data analysis by loading a sas7bdat file and then ask Positron to tell you more about it including some visualisations. 
6. Positron will produce SAS code. 
7. Ask to Export into Quarto doc - Positron will export and produce `sas` code chunks using the `sasquatch` library.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump webpack from 5.106.2 to 5.107.2
description:
Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 5.106.2 to 5.107.2.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v5.107.2

Patch Changes

  • Reduce per-file overhead in ContextModuleFactory.resolveDependencies by batching alternativeRequests hook calls. Previously the hook was invoked once per file in the context (with a single-item array), paying per-call overhead (closure allocation, resolverFactory.get, intermediate arrays in RequireContextPlugin) for every file. The hook is now invoked once per directory with all matched files in one batch — RequireContextPlugin's tap already iterates the items array, so the output is unchanged. Steady-state rebuild on a 4000-file require.context drops a further ~15 ms (after the watch-mode purge fix in the same release). (by @​alexander-akait in #21020)

  • Include each external info's runtimeCondition in ConcatenatedModule#updateHash so changes to a concatenated external's runtime condition invalidate persistent caches instead of slipping through with the module id alone. (by @​alexander-akait in #21023)

  • Fix HTML [contenthash] for referenced asset and inline-style URL changes. (by @​alexander-akait in #21018)

  • Resolve chunk-hash placeholders in chunk URLs embedded into extracted HTML. (by @​alexander-akait in #21018)

  • Remove unnecessary __webpack_require__ runtime helpers in ESM library output with multi-module chunks. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #21032)

  • Rewrite NormalModule#getSideEffectsConnectionState walk as an allocation-light iterative loop instead of a generator trampoline, restoring rebuild performance lost in #20993 while keeping deep import chains stack-safe. (by @​alexander-akait in #21014)

  • Fix runtime ReferenceError on the first activation of a lazy-compiled module when output.library.type produces a closure-wrapped bundle (umd, umd2, amd, amd-require, system). (by @​alexander-akait in #21013)

    External modules of these types reference closure-bound identifiers like __WEBPACK_EXTERNAL_MODULE_react__, supplied by the library wrapper that is generated once per chunk. When lazyCompilation activates an entry or import for the first time, any external dependency the lazily-built module pulls in arrives in a hot-update chunk that lives outside the original wrapper closure, so its factory body cannot resolve the closure identifier and only a manual page refresh recovers.

    The inactive LazyCompilationProxyModule now declares statically-enumerable externals (string and object forms of externals) as its own dependencies, so the initial entry chunk's library wrapper already exposes their closure identifiers. When activation later pulls in those externals through the lazily-compiled module, they resolve to the already-installed factories instead of throwing. Function and RegExp externals are not pre-populated because their effective request set isn't knowable up front.

  • Fill in missing entryOptions when an async block joins an existing entrypoint. (by @​alexander-akait in #21026)

  • Release per-child codeGenerationResults in MultiCompiler and at Compiler.close to reduce memory retention. (by @​alexander-akait in #21015)

  • Reduce peak memory of SourceMapDevToolPlugin on large builds (closes #20961). (by @​alexander-akait in #20963)

  • Fix slow require.context() / dynamic import() rebuilds in watch mode (#13636). When a file inside a watched context directory changed, NodeWatchFileSystem would call inputFileSystem.purge(contextDir). The enhanced-resolve purge implementation matches cache keys with key.startsWith(contextDir), so the stat cache of every file under the directory was discarded on every rebuild — ContextModuleFactory.resolveDependencies then re-stat-ed the whole tree on each rebuild. Single-file rebuilds on a 4000-file context now reuse the warm stat cache, dropping median rebuild from ~1260 ms to ~650 ms in a local reproduction (≈49%). For directory items that are explicitly watched contexts, purge is now called with { exact: true } (added in enhanced-resolve@5.22.0) so only the directory's own entry is invalidated; file-level changes in the same aggregated event continue to purge file stats and the parent readdir as before. (by @​alexander-akait in #21020)

v5.107.1

Patch Changes

  • Align the experimental HTML tokenizer with the WHATWG spec: fix offset-range bugs in the script-data, content-mode end-tag, attribute-value, and EOF states; surface tokenizer parse errors to consumers via a new parseError callback ("warning" when the tokenizer recovers and the emitted token is still well-formed, "error" when the offset range is incomplete — e.g. eof-in-tag); and add the full WHATWG named character references table so decodeHtmlEntities handles all named entities (including legacy bare forms like &AMP and multi-code-point entities like ≂̸) with proper longest-prefix backtracking. (by @​alexander-akait in #21000)

  • Tree-shake CommonJS modules imported through a const NAME = require(LITERAL) binding when only static members of NAME are read. Previously webpack treated every export of such modules as referenced (because the bare require() dependency reports EXPORTS_OBJECT_REFERENCED), so unused exports.x = ... assignments remained in the bundle even with usedExports enabled. The parser now forwards NAME.x / NAME.x() / NAME["x"] accesses to the underlying CommonJsRequireDependency as referenced exports, falling back to the full exports object the moment NAME is read in any other context (passed by value, destructured later, accessed with a dynamic key, …). This brings the binding form to parity with the existing destructuring form (const { x } = require(...)). (by @​alexander-akait in #21003)

  • Fix RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded thrown from HarmonyImportSideEffectDependency.getModuleEvaluationSideEffectsState on long linear chains of side-effect-free imports. NormalModule.getSideEffectsConnectionState previously descended through HarmonyImportSideEffectDependency.getModuleEvaluationSideEffectsState recursively, adding two stack frames per module, which overflowed V8's stack at a few thousand modules deep. The traversal is now iterative. (by @​alexander-akait in #20993)

  • Fix NormalModuleFactory parser/generator types: (by @​alexander-akait in #20999)

    • module.generator.html now uses HtmlGeneratorOptions instead of EmptyGeneratorOptions (the extract option was hidden from the createGenerator / generator hook types).
    • WebAssembly (webassembly/async, webassembly/sync) generator hooks now use EmptyGeneratorOptions instead of EmptyParserOptions.
    • NormalModuleFactory#getParser / createParser / getGenerator / createGenerator are now generic over the module-type string, returning the specific parser/generator class for known types (e.g. JavascriptParser for "javascript/auto", CssGenerator for "css", etc.) instead of always returning the base Parser / Generator.
    • NormalModuleCreateData is now generic over the module type so parser, parserOptions, generator, and generatorOptions are narrowed to the specific class / options for the given type.

  • Link import bindings used inside define(...) callbacks in ES modules. Previously, HarmonyDetectionParserPlugin skipped walking the arguments of define calls in harmony modules, so references to imported bindings inside an inline AMD define factory (e.g. define(function () { console.log(foo); })) were not rewritten to their imported references and could cause ReferenceError at runtime. Inner graph usage analysis is also fixed for the related pattern const fn = function () { foo; }; define(fn);. (by @​alexander-akait in #20990)

  • HTML-entry pipeline (experiments.html + experiments.css): emit <link rel="stylesheet"> tags for CSS chunks reachable from a <script src> entry. Previously when the bundled JS imported CSS, the resulting .css file was emitted to disk but never referenced from the extracted HTML (no <link> tag), and when splitChunks extracted CSS into sibling chunks the HTML cloned the originating <script> for each one — producing <script src="style.js"> pointing at non-existent JS filenames instead of <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">. CSS chunks are now sorted by the entrypoint's module post-order index so the <link> tags also appear in source import order, fixing the cascade ordering issue documented in html-webpack-plugin#1838 and webpack/mini-css-extract-plugin#959 for HTML-entry builds. nonce/crossorigin/referrerpolicy are copied from the originating tag onto the emitted <link>. (by @​alexander-akait in #21002)

  • Allow devtool and SourceMapDevToolPlugin (or multiple SourceMapDevToolPlugin instances) to coexist on the same asset. Previously the second instance would silently skip any asset whose info.related.sourceMap had already been set by an earlier instance, and even when it ran the asset had been rewrapped as a RawSource so no source map could be recovered — producing an empty .map file. The plugin now keeps a per-compilation stash of pristine source maps, namespaces its persistent cache entries by the options that affect output, and appends additional related.sourceMap entries instead of overwriting them. The classic workaround of pairing devtool: 'hidden-source-map' with a new webpack.SourceMapDevToolPlugin({ filename: '[file].secondary.map', noSources: true }) now produces both maps in a single build. (by @​alexander-akait in #21001)

title: Local SAS profile: re-add when lost, Add Local SAS Profile command, detection log
description:
## Summary

The automatic `local` connection profile didn't appear on the test Workbench. The cause (found live on posit.pcluster): the profile is added once, and the `SAS.localProfileAdded` flag in `globalState` keeps a deleted profile deleted. On Posit Workbench that flag outlives sessions **and browsers** (a fresh browser in a brand-new session still saw it), so once the profile was lost from `settings.json`, it was never added again, and users had no way to reset the flag.

- **Re-add a lost profile:** the flag is ignored when there are no connection profiles at all. A profile deleted in favor of another one still stays deleted.
- **`SAS: Add Local SAS Profile`:** adds the profile on request (ignoring the flag and other stdio profiles), unless a stdio profile already uses the same launcher. It reports what it did, or that no SAS was found (pointing at `SAS.localSasPaths`).
- **`SAS Local Profile` output channel:** logs where detection looked, what it found, why it skipped or added, and, 15 s after adding, whether the profile is still in `settings.json` (Workbench writes it at session start).
- **New candidate path:** `/opt/sas/viya/home/SASFoundation/bin/sas_u8`, after the Analytics Pro path. Note: the `sas/apro` image also has `SASFoundation/sas` (a symlink to `bin/sas_u8`), so this path was not the cause on the test Workbench; it covers installs without that symlink.
- Docs (`localInstalled.md`, `sas9stdio.md`, `Features/positron.md`) and CHANGELOG updated.

Seen in the same logs but not fixed here: upstream `sasDiagnostics.ts:199` throws on `window.activeTextEditor.document` when a file is saved with no active editor, and something in the bundle reads `navigator` (Positron's PendingMigrationError).

Conflict note: #170 also adds an `## Unreleased` section to CHANGELOG.md; whichever merges second needs to combine them (Features from #170, Bug Fixes from here).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test-positron` (726 passing): stale flag with no profiles re-adds; flag with other profiles skips; manual mode ignores the flag, adds next to a stdio profile with another saspath, skips one with the same saspath; log messages; candidate order
- [x] Live on posit.pcluster (demouser, `sas/apro:2026.10`): with the flag set and no profile, the first window of a new session logged "Skipped: … was added before" (the bug)
- [ ] Live: a new session with this build re-adds the profile; `SAS: Add Local SAS Profile` from the Command Palette

title: Positron: macro variables and WORK in the Variables pane (#158)
description:
Closes #158.

## Summary

Adds a SAS macro variable viewer, like the one in SAS Enterprise Guide, in Positron's **Variables** pane.

- **The pane is no longer empty for SAS.** Positron already asked every SAS session for a `positron.variables` client, but `createClient` ignored the request. The new comm (`client/src/positron/sasVariables.ts`) lists:
  - GLOBAL macro variables with their values;
  - AUTOMATIC macro variables, grouped under one expandable **Automatic macro variables** entry;
  - WORK datasets and views as `WORK.X [n obs x m vars]`, which expand to their columns and open in the Data Explorer.
- **Updates after each run**, highlighting what changed. Copying a macro variable gives `%let name=value;`, like EG's "Copy assignments". **Delete all objects** deletes the user's GLOBAL macro variables and WORK tables and keeps `POSIT_*` and `_SASPROGRAMFILE`.
- **AI agents:** Posit Assistant (1.12) reads `positron.runtime.getSessionVariables` for every prompt, so it now sees the macro variables and WORK tables. The `sas-results` skill explains the entries.
- **SAS: Evaluate Macro Expression...** is EG's quick view. It's in the Command Palette and the Variables pane's title bar. Expressions with semicolons, unbalanced quotes or parentheses, or comments are refused, because they would leave the hidden `%let` waiting for the rest of a statement.
- **`SAS.variablesPane.enabled`** (default `true`) turns the pane off.

## How the snapshot is read

- **SAS Viya:** the Compute API reads the snapshot without running SAS code, so `&SYSERR`, `&SYSCC` and `&SYSLAST` keep the values the user's code left. `GET /sessions/{id}/variables` gives the macro variables. `GET /data/WORK` plus one `GET /data/WORK/{table}` per table gives the tables, because the collection only gives names (`Accept-Item` returns 406). If this fails, the extension falls back to the SAS query below.
- **SSH and local SAS:** a hidden query runs inside a temporary macro.
  - It reads `SASHELP.VMACRO` first, before any other hidden step resets the automatic variables. VMACRO goes into a hash, because creating macro variables while reading the view can loop.
  - VMACRO supplies only the **names**. The values are written with `%superq` in `%qsubstr` chunks of 200. VMACRO holds the raw bytes of macro-quoted values, so `%str(a;b)` came out garbled.
  - The macro's locals are all named `_SAS_*`, so they can't hide a user's global of the same name.
- **Cleanup:** the existing hidden queries now `%symdel` their row and library helper globals (`_dr*`, `_sas_lib*`, `_sas_mem*`). Before, those stayed in the session and could hold up to 32K of row data each. The pane hides internal `_SAS_*` and the helper names.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: `npm run test-positron` passes (741). They cover parsing (pipes, blanks at chunk boundaries, trailing blanks, internal names), the expression check, the comm's RPCs (list, inspect, clipboard, view, delete, clear, query_table_summary, unknown method), and the update diff.
- [x] `tsc -p ./client` and eslint are clean for the changed files.
- [x] The generated SAS code ran on live SAS Viya as compute jobs, and the parsed output was compared with the Compute API. Matches: a 900-character value, a value with blanks at the 200-character boundary, `%str(a;b)`, `%str(it%'s)`, `%nrstr(&x %y)`, a value with pipes, leading blanks, a dataset label containing `|`, and a view. A user global `_i` survived, and no helper globals were left behind.
- [x] `fetchSessionSnapshot` ran against live Viya: full values were returned, and `&SYSERR` stayed at 1012 after a failed step.
- [x] Checked by hand in Positron on SAS Viya: the pane fills, the automatic group and `WORK.A` expand, the Data Explorer opens, copy works, and Evaluate works.
- [x] Positron with local SAS (stdio, `sas/apro` image) and SSH on posit.pcluster: the pane fills on a new session and after `%let`, and the console shows only the user's code (`74   %let x=1;`).

## Fixes found while testing SSH and local SAS

- **Initial list:** Positron creates the Variables client only when the session goes Ready (`positronVariablesInstance.ts` `attachRuntime`), skips its own earlier `list` requests, and never lists afterwards. The comm now sends a `refresh` event with the whole list from `createClient`.
- **stdio log routing:** with `-stdio`, SAS logs to stderr, which went to the session log, so the console printed it unfiltered and silent runs (which capture the execution log) got nothing. Once SAS is ready, stderr now goes to the execution log, as with SSH.
- **stdio end of run:** a run ended when a stderr chunk contained the end marker anywhere, so the source echo `N   %put <marker>;` ended it early, and the marker's output then ended the next run (the silent snapshot) before it logged anything. Now per line with `endsWith`, as SSH does.
- **SSH:** `stty -echo` before starting SAS (the pty echoed every submitted line, wrapper code included), and the ODS body file name is taken from the submitted code instead of that echo.
- **Wrapped log lines:** stdio and SSH start SAS with `-linesize max`. At the default ~78 columns, the submission comment and the ODS body-file note were split into pieces the console filter could not recognize. The echo of the end-marker `%put` is hidden too.

title: Variables pane: fix Positron 2026.11, group startup macro variables
description:
## Summary

**Bug fix: Variables pane empty on Positron 2026.11.** For SAS sessions on Positron 2026.11.1, the Variables pane stayed empty and its reload button spun forever. Positron 2026.12 was not affected.

- **Cause:** when a session starts, Positron 2026.11's connections service (`closeRuntimeConnections`, removed in 2026.12) calls `listClients("positron.connection")` and disposes every client it gets back. `listClients` ignored the type and returned all of the session's clients, so Positron removed the Variables comm too. Positron's later `list` requests then went unanswered.
- **Fix:** `listClients` returns only the clients of the requested type.

**Feature: "Startup macro variables" group.** The GLOBAL macro variables a session already has when it starts (`POSIT_*`, autoexec) are grouped under **Startup macro variables**, like the AUTOMATIC ones, so the user's own variables (`%let x=1;`) stand out at the top level.
- **Baseline:** the first non-empty snapshot. It is kept on the runtime session, so a comm that Positron re-creates (window reload) doesn't absorb the user's variables, and it is reset on shutdown and restart.
- **Reassigned variables:** a startup variable the user gives a new value moves to the top level.
- **Delete all objects** keeps the startup variables.

Docs (`Features/positron.md`) and the CHANGELOG (Unreleased) are updated.

## Testing

- **End to end on both Positron versions.** I ran the extension inside the real Positron 2026.11.1-4 and 2026.12.0-157 builds (positron-test-electron), with a fake `sas -stdio` script and a temporary API test that polls `positron.runtime.getSessionVariables`.
  - Before the fix, 2026.11.1 timed out on every list; 2026.12 answered.
  - After the fix, both answer at once. After `%let x=1;`, `X=1` is listed at the top level, next to the Startup and Automatic groups.
- **Unit tests:** new tests cover the startup group, reassignment, the one-time baseline, and that Clear and Delete keep startup variables. `npm run test-positron` passes (754 tests) and `tsc -p ./client` is clean.

title: Positron: SAS console commands for coding agents via the MCP server (#156)
description:
Closes #156.

## Why agents didn't see the SAS console

Positron's MCP server (Kallichore, `ai.mcp.enabled`) builds `list_sessions` / `execute_code` from the sessions the kernel supervisor manages. Those are only Jupyter kernels. The SAS console is an extension-implemented runtime, so it never appears, and agents such as Claude Code fall back to saspy.

The same server also offers agents `list_positron_commands` / `run_positron_command`. That catalog is `positron.ai.getAgentAllowedCommands()`. In Positron 2026.11 it includes extension commands whose `contributes.commands[]` entry has an `agent` block, if the publisher is trusted (`product.json` `trustedExtensionPublishers`: `posit`, `rstudio`).

## What this adds

- **`SAS.agent.listSessions`** (read-only): `{ sessions, profiles }`, i.e. the running SAS consoles (profile, connection type, foreground flag) and the connection profiles a console can start with.
- **`SAS.agent.startConsole`** (`profile` optional, not read-only, so the agent asks first): starts a console with the active or named profile, or returns the running one (`started: false`). It is a separate command rather than an implicit start inside `runCode`, for three reasons:
  - Positron's MCP session tools never start sessions either; starting is an IDE command.
  - Starting can need the user (Viya sign-in, SSH password).
  - The profile decides where code runs and which data it reaches.

  The console belongs to the user (default `owner`).
- **`SAS.agent.runCode`** (`code`, optional `sessionId`): runs the code in the foreground (or named) SAS console through `positron.runtime.executeCode`, so it shows in the console and history and shares WORK and macro variables. It returns `{ sessionId, log, result, error?, clipped }`:
  - `log` is the console's stream text.
  - `result` is the `text/plain` copy of the report.
  - `error` is the runtime error message.
  - Positron refuses replies over 32 KB of JSON unless it can shorten an array, so `log` and `result` are clipped to 28 KB together. The clip keeps the head and the tail.
- No `enablement`. Without a console, `runCode` fails with a message telling the agent to ask the user, then use `startConsole`, and not to use saspy.
- All three commands are hidden from the Command Palette. Older Positron versions ignore the `agent` block.
- Docs: new "Other Coding Agents" section in `website/docs/Features/positron.md`, plus a CHANGELOG entry.

## Testing

- Unit tests for clipping and error text (`client/test/positron/agentReply.test.ts`): `npm run test-positron` passes (792).
- New Positron API test (`client/test/positron-api/agent-commands.test.ts`):
  - the commands are in `getAgentAllowedCommands`, `listSessions` is `readOnly`, and `startConsole` is not;
  - run through `validateAndExecuteCommand`, the same call the MCP channel makes, they return no sessions, the "No SAS console" error, and an error for an unknown profile.
- Local live run (Positron 2026.11.1-4, fake `sas -stdio`, temporary test not committed), all through `validateAndExecuteCommand`:
  - `listSessions` returned the console;
  - `runCode` returned the log;
  - a SAS ERROR came back in `log` and `error`;
  - a 5000-line log was clipped to a 28 KB reply;
  - an unknown `sessionId` gave a clear error;
  - `startConsole("fake")` started a console in about 0.6 s, `runCode` then ran in it, and a second `startConsole` returned it with `started: false`.
- **Not yet checked:**
  - the real Kallichore MCP transport with Claude Code against a real SAS console;
  - whether `run_positron_command` times out while a slow Viya start (sign-in) is in progress.

title: stdio and SSH: detect the SAS session encoding (#182)
description:
Closes #182.

The stdio and SSH connections assumed UTF-8 everywhere: output was decoded with `data.toString()`, code was written as UTF-8, and the docs and local-profile detection insisted on `bin/sas_u8`. Sites whose data is in WLATIN1 or LATIN1 had to choose between CEDA and transcoding problems on their data (`sas_u8`) or garbled non-ASCII text (their own launcher).

## What changes

- **Detection:** the startup data step that prints the WORK path now also prints `&SYSENCODING` (`SASENC…SASENCEND`). Setup finishes once it arrives; if it doesn't within 30 s, or names an encoding without a codec, the session goes on with UTF-8 and logs a warning.
- **Decoding and encoding** (new `client/src/connection/encoding.ts`, using `iconv-lite`, bundled):
  - Each output stream has its own stateful decoder. This also fixes multi-byte characters split across chunks, in UTF-8 sessions too.
  - Code is encoded in the session encoding. A UTF-8 session still gets the plain string, so nothing changes there.
  - Characters the encoding lacks become `?`, with a warning in the log.
- **HTML results** are decoded by their `charset` meta tag, falling back to the session encoding.
- **Setup waits for the system variables.** It no longer resolves at the prompt. This removes the race where the first run's results were missed because the WORK folder wasn't known yet.
- **Local profile:** for SAS 9.4, detection now tries each install's `sas` script (the site's configured encoding) before `bin/sas_u8`. **Add Local SAS Profile** treats `sas` and `bin/sas_*` of one install as the same, so it adds no duplicate.
- **No new setting:** the launcher, or `-encoding` in `sasOptions`, decides.
- **Docs:** new "Session Encoding" section in `sas9stdio.md`; `sas9ssh.md`, `localInstalled.md` and `positron.md` updated; CHANGELOG entry.

## Live check (SAS Analytics Pro image, throwaway Workbench session)

I ran SAS with the extension's startup code under every launcher in `SASFoundation/bin`, plus `-encoding latin1` and `-encoding wlatin1`:

- **Encoding names:** each reported its encoding in the expected format (`SASENCwlatin1 SASENCEND`): utf-8, latin1, wlatin1, latin9, latin2, latin5, arabic, cyrillic, hebrew, euc-jp, shift-jis, euc-kr, euc-cn and ms-950 all map to a codec. Only `sas_zt.euc` (euc-tw) has none, so it falls back to UTF-8 with a warning.
- **ODS HTML5 always writes UTF-8** with `<meta charset="utf-8"/>`, whatever the session encoding. That's why results are decoded by the charset tag first.

Not yet checked end to end: the built extension against a real non-UTF-8 session. The stdio and SSH paths are covered by unit tests: wlatin1 log decoding, code written as single bytes, chunk-split tags, the timeout fallback, and closing before the tag arrives.

## Notes

- The docs say non-UTF-8 sessions need any version later than 1.2.1. This PR doesn't bump the version, so merging doesn't release anything.

title: Quarto: syntax highlighting for {sas} chunks in rendered documents (#174)
description:
Closes #174.

## Cause

Two things keep `{sas}` chunk code plain in rendered Quarto documents:

1. **sasquatch labels the code `txt`.** Its knitr engine starts with `options$engine <- "txt"`. This is in 0.1.3 and in current `ropensci/sasquatch` main. Every SAS source block therefore becomes ```` ```{.txt .cell-code} ````. Adding `class-source: sas` doesn't help: Pandoc takes `txt` as a known plain syntax, so `.txt .sas` stays unhighlighted, while `.foo .sas` and `.sas .txt` are highlighted.
2. **Older Pandoc has no SAS grammar.** skylighting 0.15 added one (from KDE's `sas.xml`), and Pandoc 3.12+ uses it. Quarto 1.11.9 bundles Pandoc 3.10, without SAS. Quarto 1.12.x bundles 3.13, with SAS.

## Changes

- **Docs** (`Features/positron.md`): a new section, "Syntax Highlighting in Rendered Documents", with:
  - a 4-line wrapper for the `setup` chunk that renames the fence to `.sas`
  - the `syntax-definitions: [sas.xml]` workaround for Quarto 1.11 and earlier, linking a pinned KDE commit
  - a bullet for it in the list of report rules
- **`sas-quarto-report` skill** and the matching `SAS Quarto Integration` assistant context: reports from Posit Assistant include the wrapper in their `setup` chunk. Nothing is added for older Quarto unless the user asks.
- CHANGELOG entry.

If sasquatch later labels the code `sas` itself, the wrapper finds no `.txt` fence and has no effect.

title: Faster Data Explorer for SAS datasets (#177)
description:
Closes #177.

The Variables pane and the Connections / Data Connections panes open SAS datasets through the same Data Explorer backend (`openDataExplorer` → `SasDataExplorer`), so this PR speeds up that backend; it doesn't matter which pane opened the table. Each hidden SAS query is a full job round trip (on Viya: submit, poll, log, results), and jobs run one at a time, so the time to first rows was roughly *jobs × job latency*.

## Changes

One commit each, so the two upstream-file changes (REST, ITC) can be dropped on their own:

1. **Data Explorer** (`sasClient.ts`, `sasDataExplorer.ts`)
   - Opening a dataset is **one job instead of four**. `openDataset` reads the type, change stamp, columns, row count and the first 50 rows of up to 50 columns in one job. Before, there were separate jobs for the columns, the `count(*)`, the stamp and the rows.
   - Dictionary lookups use `libname=`/`memname=` equality instead of `upcase()`, which made SAS scan the metadata of every assigned library.
   - Rows are cached in blocks of 50 per column. A request reads only the missing columns of the missing blocks, and concurrent requests share one read. Blocks are small because every row read is a log line that has to come back: with blocks of 200, a scroll to row 2000 read 400 rows and took about 1 s.
   - With a sort or filter, the first read creates a hidden `WORK._SASDVn` table holding the sorted and filtered rows and returns the page from it **in the same job**, which costs what 1.2.1's sort into a throwaway table did. Later pages are read from that table without sorting again. It's dropped with the next sort or filter, on refresh and on dispose, and the Variables and Connections panes don't list it.
   - Column profiles take **2 jobs instead of 6**. `SasClient` hands one job at a time to the session and lets foreground jobs (rows, counts) overtake background ones (profiles). Before starting a background job it waits one turn, so a row read that follows another isn't held up by a profile job started in between. Waiting jobs also no longer fill the session's 10-job silent queue or get rejected from it when the user runs code.
   - Rows go to the log in 200-character chunks, as the Variables snapshot already does, so log line wrapping can't split a wide row. This is a safeguard only: wide rows weren't losing values with 1.2.1 in the timing run.
2. **Viya REST:** silent jobs skip the ODS-results GET, so each makes one HTTP request fewer.
3. **ITC (SAS 9 IOM/COM):** the log is polled after 100 ms, doubling up to the old 2 s, instead of a fixed 2 s interval. Every hidden query used to take at least 2 s. This also fixes the interval leaking when a run started within 2 s of the previous one. There's no IOM server to test against, so this is covered by unit tests only.
4. **Docs and CHANGELOG.**

## Timing (test Workbench, SAS Viya, `WORK.BIG`: 100,000 rows × 28 columns)

Measured with Playwright, in milliseconds from the click to the first frame where the condition held. **1.2.1** is the release, measured on the same day as **dev** (this branch, at `eb22d338`). The earlier 1.2.1 runs (Nov 21) gave the same picture.

| Measurement | 1.2.1 (median) | dev (median) |
|---|---|---|
| Variables pane: view icon → first cell | 2631, 2698, 2415 (**2631**) | 749, 781, 1098 (**781**) |
| Histograms visible (same click) | 2958, 3036, 2737 (**2958**) | 1536, 1536, 1934 (**1536**) |
| Data Connections: Open in Data Explorer → first cell | Nov 21: **2633**, **2484** | 749, 864, 816 (**816**) |
| Histograms (Data Connections) | Nov 21: **2989**, **2822** | 1536, 1654, 1610 (**1610**) |
| One hidden job (expand a table in the Variables pane) | Nov 21: **411**, **416** | 318, 332, 336, 317 (**325**) |
| Sort ascending (x1, x2, x3) until the cells change | 866, 1014, 1264 (**1014**) | 533, 678, 1543 (**678**) |
| Sort right after opening (sort check, x4, x5) | 1862, 1881 | 927, 911 |
| Sort again after clearing it (x4, x5) | 565, 565 | 563, 532 |
| Sort, then scroll down 2000 rows at once (x7, x8, x9) | 2732, 2867, 2967 (**2867**) | 933, 1567, 1034 (**1034**) |
| Scroll down 2000 rows, 1.5 s after a sort | 468, 532, 1150 (**532**) | 485, 1181, 1101 (**1101**) |

- **Opening is about 3× faster from both panes**, and the histograms appear about 1.4 s sooner.
- **Sorting is faster**, and scrolling a sorted table doesn't sort it again: a sort followed by a scroll takes about 1 s instead of about 2.9 s.
- **Each hidden job is about 90 ms faster**, from skipping the ODS-results request.
- **Scrolling right after opening can wait for one profile job.** The summary panel asks for profiles one batch after another for about 8 s after opening, and a job SAS is running can't be interrupted. A trace of the jobs showed the slow scrolls (about 1.1 s) waiting for a histogram-count job of about 1.3 s that was already running; the scroll's own read took about 0.4 s. In 1.2.1 those profile jobs ran before the first rows instead, which is part of why opening took 2.6 s. Making the histogram-count query cheaper would shorten this wait; that's left for a follow-up.
- Scrolling back up was already instant (5–15 ms) in both, because Positron keeps rows on its side.
- No operation came close to the 10 s log-poll stall we suspected.

### How the sort got here

The first version of this branch built the sorted table in a separate job before reading the page, which made a new sort slower than 1.2.1 (about 2.9 s against 0.8 s). Building it in the background instead (`58a68f8f`) didn't help: when SAS was idle the build started first, so the first page waited for one full sort and then ran its own. `eb22d338` builds the table and reads the page in one job, and also fixes the gap that let profile jobs slip in between two row reads.

## Tests

- `npm run test-positron`: 784 passing, including new tests for the one-job open, the row cache, view tables (built with the first page, waited for while building, fallback when they can't be built), the job queue (including the turn before a background job), the combined profile query and the chunked rows.

title: SSH: connect to SAS 9.4 on Windows through the ITC PowerShell bridge
description:
## Why

Users on Positron (Linux) need to reach SAS 9.4 on a Windows server. The `ssh` connection can't drive SAS on Windows:

- It types `stty -echo; env … sas -nodms -noterminal` into a shell, and reads results with `cat`. None of that exists on Windows.
- SAS on Windows has no stdin/stdout line mode: `-stdio` is UNIX-only and `-nodms` isn't valid there. saspy's STDIO-over-SSH has the same limit; it only supports SAS on Linux.

## What

For an `ssh` profile whose `saspath` looks like Windows (drive letter, backslash or `.exe`), or with `"platform": "windows"`, the extension now runs the **COM connection's PowerShell bridge (`itc.ps1`) on the server**, over an ssh2 `exec` channel. The bridge starts SAS through SAS Integration Technologies, so SAS keeps its state between runs. We also get ITC's log line types, cancel (Positron interrupt), and the Libraries and Server Files views.

- **`ITCSession`** (upstream file, small seams):
  - `openShell()`: the local spawn stays synchronous, so the upstream tests' timing is unchanged.
  - a `remote` flag
  - an overridable results fetch (`fetchResultsFile` / `displayResults`)
- **`getScript({ remote })`**:
  - inlines `env.json`, which `itc.ps1` would otherwise read from `$PWD`
  - drops `Set-Location`
  - appends the new `itcRemote.ps1`, whose functions send results and server files as base64 on stdout
  - `itc.ps1` itself is unchanged
- **`ssh/windows.ts`** (`SSHWindowsSession extends ITCSession`):
  - runs `cmd /d /c "chcp 65001 >NUL & powershell.exe -NonInteractive -NoProfile -Command -"`, which works whether the server's OpenSSH default shell is cmd or PowerShell
  - a byte-level line splitter, because SSH packets split long lines and UTF-8 characters
  - base64 results kept out of the log
  - startup-only `sasOptions` (e.g. `-nosplash`, `-noicon`) are dropped with a warning. COM's `SetOptions` can't set them after SAS starts.
  - `"windowsProtocol": "iom"` (`iomPort`, default 8591) is the fallback if DCOM won't start SAS for an SSH login. It connects over IOM Bridge to the server's own object spawner.
- **`ssh/connect.ts`**: the SSH auth middleware for the new session, the same logic as `SSHSession`. `SSHSession` itself is untouched, so existing SSH users aren't affected.
- **Views**: `viewConnectionType()` maps these profiles to the COM adapters for Libraries and Server Files. Server file downloads use base64 instead of a local temp file.
- **saspy export**: these profiles are written as saspy IOM configurations.
- **Profile schema**: new `platform`, `windowsProtocol`, `iomPort` and `interopLibraryFolderPath`. `saspath` is no longer required by the schema; validation still requires it unless `platform` is `windows`.
- Docs (`sas9ssh.md`: requirements, profile, troubleshooting) and CHANGELOG.
- **Probe script** `doc/scripts/ssh-windows-probe.ps1`: it runs over SSH the way the extension does (`cmd /c chcp`, `powershell -Command -` on stdin) and reports on:
  - PowerShell language mode and the SSH logon type
  - the SAS COM registration, where `SASInterop.dll` is, and the SAS IOM data provider
  - the object spawner port, and an optional network path
  - a test SAS session over COM done exactly as the extension's Setup does (in a job with a timeout), including reading an ODS file through the FileService as `itcRemote.ps1` does

  It ends with findings that map to profile settings. It was checked statically only (balanced braces; no `catch`/`else` starting a line, which breaks stdin input). It hasn't been run, as there is no PowerShell here.

## Testing

- `client/test/positron/sshWindows.test.ts` (runs in `test-positron`): detection, view mapping, option normalization, remote script assembly against the real `itc.ps1`, saspy export. `npm run test-positron`: 805 passing.
- `client/test/connection/ssh/windows.test.ts` (runs in `test-client`), with ssh2 `Client` and the channel stubbed. It covers:
  - the exec command and the Setup lines for COM and IOM
  - work dir and setup
  - results base64 split across packets with a multibyte character, kept out of the log
  - closing, and a connection that closes during setup

  Run locally under mocha with a catch-all `vscode` mock: 6/6 pass. The existing ITC/SSH suites have the same results as on `main` under that mock; 4 tests fail there only because the mock lacks `workspace.fs` and the real script path.
- `tsc -p client` (tests included) and eslint on the touched files are clean.
- **Verified live (2026-11-25)** by a user on Positron (Linux) against SAS 9.4 on Windows Server 2019, with the dev VSIX and `"windowsProtocol": "iom"`. The profile used the bare user ID with key authentication; the spawner on `localhost:8591` accepted it.
- **What the probe found on that server**: `"com"` is denied for SSH logins (`0x80070005`; the login is in `NETWORK`, not `INTERACTIVE`). The docs now explain the DCOM permission an administrator can grant, and when to use `iom` instead.
- **Still unverified live**:
  - `"com"` on a server that allows it
  - the Libraries and Server Files views (confirmed past merge)
  - interrupt
  - whether SAS processes are left behind if SSH drops

title: Run SAS programs as Posit Workbench Jobs with sasjob
description:
## Summary

In a Posit Workbench session, **Run Script in a Workbench Job** now works on `.sas` files, from the editor's run menu or the Explorer. The job runs the program on SAS Viya with `sasjob`. The **Workbench Jobs** view streams the SAS log while it runs, the program keeps running after Positron is closed, and it can be stopped from the view.

This depends on rstudio/rstudio-workbench-vscode-ext#543, which adds a `registerScriptType()` API to the Posit Workbench extension. Without that API, nothing changes: the extension logs that SAS programs can't run as Workbench Jobs.

## How it works

- `client/src/workbenchJobs/index.ts` registers the `sas` script type when the Workbench extension is present and exposes `apiVersion: 1`. It doesn't wait for that extension to activate.
- `client/src/workbenchJobs/sasjob.ts` is free of the vscode API and unit tested. It resolves the command as `sasjob run <args> <program>`. The default arguments come from the active SAS Viya profile:
  - `--viya-url` from the endpoint
  - `--integration`, `--context` and `--sas-option` when the profile sets them (options in Compute form, e.g. `-PAGESIZE MAX`)
  - one `--autoexec-line` per autoexec line
- The dialog warns when no SAS Viya profile is active, when the profile signs in with SAS Logon (a job uses the Workbench OAuth integration instead), and when the job runs on a non-local cluster, where `sasjob` must be installed.
- New setting: `SAS.workbenchJobs.sasjobPath` (default `sasjob`).
- `client/src/workbenchJobs/posit-workbench-api.ts` is a verbatim copy of the Workbench extension's `src/api.ts`.
- Docs: a "Run SAS Programs as Workbench Jobs" section in `website/docs/Workbench/Positron/remoteViya.md`, and a CHANGELOG entry.

## Testing

- `client/test/positron/workbenchJobs.test.ts` covers argument building and the warnings. All 817 Positron unit tests pass. Locally I ran them with `TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY`, because `describe` types don't resolve in my environment; that happens on `main` too.
- ESLint and `tsc` pass on the changed files.
- Manual check in a Workbench session with both VSIXs: choosing a `.sas` file opens the job dialog with `sasjob` and `--viya-url` filled in.
- _End-to-end job run on SAS Viya (log streaming, stop, exit status): to follow._

title: saspy export: SAS Viya token from a Posit Connect Service Account integration
description:
## Problem

A Quarto document that uses sasquatch/saspy with an exported SAS Viya configuration renders on Workbench, but fails on Posit Connect:

```
Error in `py_call_impl()`:
! EOFError: EOF when reading a line
```

The configuration had no token source on Connect, so saspy asked for a user ID with `input()`, and a render has no stdin.

## Change

- **Token from Connect:** on Connect, the exported `sascfg_personal.py` exchanges the content session token for the token of the content's OAuth integration. It reads `CONNECT_CONTENT_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE` first, which Connect refreshes, then `CONNECT_CONTENT_SESSION_TOKEN`. The request is the same one posit-sdk's `get_content_credentials()` sends, made with Python's standard library, so the content needs no extra package. `SAS_VIYA_CONNECT_INTEGRATION_ID` picks one integration when the content has several.
- **Context for tokens without a user:** a Service Account integration uses the client credentials grant, so its token has no user. SAS Compute refuses such a token in the standard contexts ("does not have permission to launch a process"). Tokens without `user_name`, from any source, now use the context `Posit Connect compute context`, which runs as a service account (`runServerAs`). `SAS_VIYA_CONNECT_CONTEXT` names another context. This also covers `SAS_VIYA_TOKEN` set from `connectapi::get_oauth_content_credentials()`.
- **Viewer integrations (Shiny):** Shiny apps in R and Python need no code. Shiny for Python: the configuration reads the token from `shiny.session.get_current_session().http_conn.headers`, which also works in threads from `asyncio.to_thread()`. R Shiny apps need no code either. When saspy connects from a reactive context, the configuration reads the viewer's session token from the Shiny session through reticulate's `r` object (`shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()`). It only does this on Connect and when shiny is already loaded. Other apps pass the token on as `CONNECT_USER_SESSION_TOKEN` on the Python main module. The configuration exchanges it as a `user-session-token`. Without it, the configuration falls back to the content session token. If the content has only a Viewer integration and no viewer token is passed, Connect answers with code 252 ("Invalid subject_token_type for the integration's specified auth_type"), and the error now says so instead of asking for a Service Account integration.
- **Workbench integration without an ID:** when neither `SAS_VIYA_INTEGRATION_ID` nor the profile names the integration, the configuration uses the one Workbench integration whose token URL is the server's SAS Logon token URL. That's the same rule as `findIntegration()` for the extension's own sign-in. Before, a Shiny app in a Workbench session got no token and saspy prompted.
- **Fix: posit-sdk client kept in a variable:** the Workbench step called `Client().oauth.get_credentials()` on a temporary client. posit-sdk 0.17.0 resources hold only a weak reference to their client, so this always failed with `ReferenceError: weakly-referenced object no longer exists`, and the template swallowed the error. Connect's `Client` behaves the same way, so the Python examples in the docs now keep the client in a variable too.
- **Clear error:** without an integration, connecting fails with a message that says to add the Service Account integration, instead of the `EOFError`.
- **Docs:** `viyaOauth.md` replaces the warning about client credentials tokens with the SAS Viya setup they need, and adds the `scopes` setting the Service Account integration needs.
- **Overview in the docs:** a new section in `viyaOauth.md`, "With the Exported saspy Configuration", has a table of token source, SAS identity and compute context for Workbench sessions, rendered Connect content and Shiny apps on Connect.
- **Other docs and the assistant:** `Features/positron.md`, `Code/index.md`, the `sas-quarto-report` skill and the assistant's setup instructions now include the Connect step. The skill also explains the Connect errors. `viyaOauth.md` now points to the **Access** tab for integrations (Settings > Access > Integrations in Connect 2026.09); it said **Runtime** before.

## Testing

- Unit tests: `saspyConfig.test.ts` and `sshWindows.test.ts` pass (31). `tsc -p ./client --noEmit` reports no errors in `client/src`.
- I ran the generated configuration against a mock Connect endpoint. It sends the posit-sdk request and reads the token file before the variable. It picks the service account context for client tokens, including ones from `SAS_VIYA_TOKEN`, and the profile's context for user tokens. Without an integration, it fails with the new error.
- Workbench lookup: tested with a stub `posit.workbench` module (one match, explicit ID, a token URL that only differs in case, default port and trailing slash, two matches, no match). Tested for real in a Workbench 2026.09 session: the configuration found the "SAS Viya" integration by its token URL and got the user's token, which uses the profile's context. A temporary `Client()` raised `ReferenceError` there.
- Viewer exchange, tested against a mock Connect: a viewer token on `__main__` takes precedence, R's `NULL` falls back to the content token, and each failure gets its own error message. The code 252 text matches what real Connect 2026.09 returned for a Shiny app with only a Viewer integration.
- Shiny lookup, tested in R (reticulate 1.47.0) against a mock Connect. With no shiny loaded, or outside a reactive context, the content session token is exchanged. Inside a viewer's reactive domain the viewer's token is exchanged, and an explicit `CONNECT_USER_SESSION_TOKEN` wins.
- Shiny for Python lookup, tested with py-shiny 1.9.0 against a mock Connect. Inside `session_context()`, and in a thread from `asyncio.to_thread()`, the viewer's token is exchanged; without a current session, the content session token.
- End to end on a SAS Viya 4 and Connect 2026.09 deployment: a Quarto document with sasquatch renders on Connect with the "SAS Viya (Service Account)" integration, and SAS runs as the service account.

title: SAS Server: show an empty start folder for IOM and local profiles
description:
Fixes #196.

## Problem

With a SAS 9.4 (remote - IOM) or (local) profile, expanding **SAS Server** failed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parentFolderUri')` when the start folder was empty. That happens, for example, with a new home folder under the default `fileNavigationRoot` (`USER`), or with an empty `CUSTOM` folder.

`FileService.ListFiles` returns the folder it listed, but `GetChildItems` in `itc.ps1` passed that path on only inside each item (`parentFolderUri`). For an empty folder the response was `{"success": true, "data": []}`, and `ItcServerAdapter.getChildItems` read `items[0].parentFolderUri`.

## Change

- `itc.ps1`: `GetItemsAtPath` returns `@{ listedPath; items }`. `GetChildItems` adds `listedPath` to its response, and the two other callers (item lookup and recursive delete) use `.items`.
- `ItcServerAdapter`: builds the Home node from `listedPath`, falling back to `items[0].parentFolderUri`. `??` keeps the `""` path of the `SYSTEM` root. If neither exists, it logs a warning and returns no items instead of throwing.
  - Hiding Home for an empty folder, as the issue suggested, would leave no place to create or upload the first file, so Home is still shown.
- New `ItcServerAdapter.test.ts` with 6 cases.
- Docs: `accessServer.md` no longer says SAS Server needs SAS Viya. `sas9iom.md` points to the file navigation root settings.

## Testing

- `npm run test-client`: 1166 passing, 3 pending.
- Old and new `itc.ps1` run in PowerShell 7 against a mock `FileService` with stub `SAS.*` enums:
  - The old script returns `{"data":[],"success":true}` for an empty home folder. The new one adds `listedPath`.
  - `SYSTEM`, `CUSTOM` (existing and missing), item lookup and recursive delete give the same results as before.
- Not tested: Windows PowerShell 5.1 and a real SAS 9.4 IOM server. I'm asking the reporter to try a pre-release VSIX of this branch.

The same code is in upstream sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension.

title: Name the extension SAS Extension for Positron in the UI and docs
description:
Replaces the remaining references to *SAS Extension for Visual Studio Code* that mean **this** extension with *SAS Extension for Positron*.

Changed:
- UI strings `views.SAS.welcome` and `views.SAS.unsupportedConnection` in `package.nls.json` and all 10 locales. The product name stays in English, as before. In Korean the object particle changes from 를 to 을, because "Positron" ends in a consonant.
- `itc.ps1`: the IOM/COM `ApplicationName`, which is the name SAS admins see for the client session, plus the same name in the SSH-to-Windows probe script.
- README and docs home: the feature list ("The SAS Extension for Positron includes the following features"). The upstream name is normalized to "SAS Extension for Visual Studio Code" where the text means upstream.
- `matrix.md` table header. The SAS 9.4 IOM/local profile pages drop the "if you are running v1.15 or later" note, because that version number is upstream's and every release of this extension is later than it.
- The Workbench overview sentence, and the contributing/locale sections of `doc/README.md`.

Docs steps that happen in the editor now say Positron: the status bar, activity bar and `settings.json` on the configuration pages; the sign-in prompts and Accounts menu in `running.md`; notebooks; the SSH, stdio, IOM and local profile pages; the FAQ (restarts, certificates, keyboard shortcuts with the macOS menu `Positron > Settings`, the `positron-server` remote processes); and the stdio README. The menu name and the server process name were checked against Positron's `product.json`.

The FAQ's "enter a GitHub issue" link now points to this repository's issue templates instead of sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension.

Kept on purpose, because these places mean upstream's extension:
- The CHANGELOG lines that give the upstream base ("based on SAS Extension for VS Code 1.21.0").
- The `vscode/` copies of upstream's README, CHANGELOG, SUPPORT and CONTRIBUTING files.
- The "Builds on the SAS Extension for Visual Studio Code" note on the Positron page, and the install section for SAS's own extension in VS Code.
- The `--vscode-sas-extension-*` log marker strings. These are protocol markers, not names, and they are shared with the upstream code and tests.
- Links to the `sassoftware/vscode-sas-extension` repository.

The edits to the upstream-shared `package.nls.*.json` and `itc.ps1` are single-line changes, so any upstream sync conflict there is trivial.
